laws.title: Drunk Driving — Zero Tolerance .03% BAC
laws.subtitle: Road Traffic Act — Yoon Chang-ho Act 2019
laws.fullDescription: South Korea dramatically tightened its DUI law in 2019. BAC limit reduced from 0.05% to 0.03%. Above 0.08% is criminal. Refusing a sobriety test results in same punishment as failing.
laws.penalty: 0.03–0.08%: licence suspension 100 days, fines up to ₩5 million. 0.08%+: up to 5 years imprisonment or ₩20 million fine.
exceptions: None — no exemptions

quiz.q: South Korea's BAC limit since 2019?
quiz.explanation: South Korea lowered its BAC limit to 0.03% in 2019.

laws.title: Korean Hierarchy — Formal Speech and Age Respect
laws.subtitle: 존댓말 (jondaemal) with elders; two-hand customs
laws.fullDescription: Always use formal speech (존댓말, jondaemal) with older people and superiors. Never use informal speech (반말, banmal) unless invited. Exchange business cards and gifts with both hands. Bow when greeting — deeper for more respect. Wait for elders to begin eating before you start. Pour drinks for others before yourself.
laws.penalty: Not legal — but using informal speech with superiors or not respecting hierarchy causes serious social harm.
exceptions: Close friends of same age may use informal speech by mutual agreement
Children addressed informally

quiz.q: What is the formal speech level in Korean called?
quiz.explanation: 존댓말 (jondaemal) is the formal/polite speech level used with elders and superiors.

laws.title: Online Defamation — Criminal Offense
laws.subtitle: Information and Communications Network Act §70 — Up to 7 years
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's online defamation law (Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection, §70) makes it a criminal offense to defame someone online — even with TRUE statements if posted with intent to harm reputation. This is significantly stricter than most Western countries. Social media posts, comments, and articles can all trigger prosecution.
laws.penalty: False information: up to 7 years imprisonment or ₩50 million fine. True but harmful: up to 5 years or ₩30 million fine.
exceptions: Public interest journalism with factual reporting has some protection
Criticism of public figures has limited protection compared to private individuals

quiz.q: In South Korea, posting TRUE but reputationally harmful information online is:
quiz.explanation: South Korea's online defamation law criminalises even TRUE statements posted online if made with intent to harm someone's reputation — up to 5 years imprisonment.

laws.title: Anti-Stalking Law — Stalking Crime Act 2021
laws.subtitle: Stalking Crimes Punishment Act — up to 5 years
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted its first dedicated anti-stalking law in 2021 (Stalking Crimes Punishment Act). Before this, only minor fines applied. The law covers repeated unwanted contact: following, loitering near home, monitoring, contacting through third parties, and digital stalking (sending messages, monitoring social media). Repeat violations can result in pre-trial detention.
laws.penalty: Stalking: up to 3 years or ₩30 million fine. Stalking with weapon/threats: up to 5 years or ₩50 million fine. Repeat: possible detention.
exceptions: Emergency restraining orders can be issued immediately
Law covers both physical and digital stalking behaviors

quiz.q: When was South Korea's first dedicated anti-stalking law enacted?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's first dedicated Stalking Crimes Punishment Act was enacted in 2021 — before that, stalking only attracted minor fines.

laws.title: Residential Noise Curfew — Late Night Hours
laws.subtitle: Noise Vibration Control Act + Apartment Regulations
laws.fullDescription: Korea strictly regulates noise in residential areas. Between 10pm and 6am (the quiet hours), residents are prohibited from making excessive noise. High-rise apartment buildings (80%+ of Seoul's population lives in apartments) have additional rules prohibiting floor-impact noise. Floor noise (뛰거나 걷는 소리, running/stomping) between neighbors is a major social issue prosecuted through the National Noise Conflict Management Service (층간소음이웃사이센터).
laws.penalty: Violations of Noise Vibration Control Act: ₩300,000–₩1 million fine. Apartment floor noise: civil mediation required, can escalate to criminal nuisance charges.
exceptions: Permitted construction hours (typically 7am–6pm weekdays)
Registered noise-producing businesses have separate permits
laws.sourceLabel: Noise and Vibration Control Act — Korea

quiz.q: What is the quiet hours period in Korean residential buildings?
quiz.explanation: Korea's residential quiet hours run from 10pm to 6am, with apartment floor noise being a major regulated issue.

laws.title: Pedestrian Safety Zone Act — School & Silver Zones
laws.subtitle: Road Traffic Act — Heavy fines near schools and elderly zones
laws.fullDescription: Korea established strict penalties for drivers in School Protection Zones (어린이보호구역, 30km/h limit) and Senior/Silver Protection Zones (노인보호구역, 30km/h). In these zones, speeding or ignoring traffic signals results in doubled penalties. The Minshikeubeop law (2019) introduced mandatory prison terms for causing injury or death in school zones.
laws.penalty: Speeding in school zone: minimum ₩130,000, up to criminal charges. Death by negligent driving in school zone: 3–15 years imprisonment (Minshikeubeop law).
exceptions: Designated school hours for school zone restrictions (typically 7am–8pm)
Silver zones active 24/7

quiz.q: What speed limit applies in Korean school protection zones?
quiz.explanation: Korean school protection zones (어린이보호구역) enforce a 30km/h speed limit, with doubled fines and criminal penalties for accidents.

laws.title: Mandatory Military Service — 18–21 Months
laws.subtitle: Military Service Act — All male citizens 18–28
laws.fullDescription: All male South Korean citizens must complete mandatory military service between the ages of 18 and 28. Service lasts 18–21 months depending on the branch (Army: 18 months, Navy: 20, Air Force: 21). The obligation applies to overseas Koreans and even dual citizens who have Korean citizenship. Korean-American men with Korean citizenship are subject to this law.
laws.penalty: Evasion: up to 3 years imprisonment. Failing to report: civil and criminal penalties. Loss of certain civil rights.
exceptions: Men with specific disabilities are exempt or assigned public service alternative
Artists/athletes who win international prizes may be exempt (e.g. Olympic medal, international music competition)
laws.sourceLabel: Military Service Act — Republic of Korea

quiz.q: How long is mandatory military service for South Korean Army soldiers?
quiz.explanation: South Korean Army mandatory service is 18 months. Navy is 20 months and Air Force is 21 months.

laws.title: Seoul Subway Etiquette — Strict Unwritten Rules
laws.subtitle: Priority seats, food bans, phone volume, elderly respect
laws.fullDescription: Seoul's subway system (세계 최고의 지하철) has firm etiquette rules. Priority seats (노약자석, pink/blue marked) near doors are for elderly, disabled, and pregnant — never sit in them even if empty. Eating is strongly frowned upon. Phone calls should be brief and quiet. Backpacks go in front during crowded times. The elderly (노인) always get offered seats. Silence in carriages is the norm — AirPod usage is fine, audible speakers are very rude.
laws.penalty: No direct legal penalty for etiquette violations — but confrontations with elderly passengers can escalate significantly and social pressure is very strong.
exceptions: Express trains have slightly different norms
Early morning trains are quieter still

quiz.q: What should you do with priority seats on Seoul's subway, even if they're empty?
options: Sit in them if no elderly person is around
Only sit if it's rush hour
They are for anyone during off-peak hours
quiz.explanation: Priority seats on Seoul's subway (노약자석) should be left empty at all times — it is considered very disrespectful to sit in them even when no elderly or disabled passengers are present.

laws.title: Age-Based Hierarchy and Honorifics — ‘Korean Age’ Replaced in 2023
laws.subtitle: Act on the Enforcement of Age Counting Method (2023) — International age now standard
laws.fullDescription: South Korean society has one of the most hierarchical age systems in the world. Koreans traditionally counted two different ‘ages’: Korean Age (Han-guk nai: born = 1, +1 every Lunar New Year — so a baby born on 31 December is instantly 2) and ‘year-counting age’ (yeonnai: calendar years minus birth year). The ‘Act on the Enforcement of Age Counting Method’ took effect on 28 June 2023, making the international age (full years lived) the default for all administrative and contractual purposes. Socially, however, knowing the other person’s year of birth remains vital: speech levels (jondaetmal honorific vs. banmal casual), seating order at meals, who pours the first drink, and who bows first all depend on relative age. Asking ‘what year were you born?’ early in a conversation is normal and polite rather than intrusive. Younger people address elders as hyung/oppa (older brother, male/female speaker), eonni/nuna (older sister, male/female speaker), and use -nim suffix for deference.
laws.penalty: No legal penalty for informal-speech breaches. Failure to use proper age-respectful speech in formal or professional settings can seriously damage relationships; the 2023 Age Counting Act is purely administrative.
exceptions: International contexts with foreigners, where English or informal norms apply
Traditional Korean calendars and some birthdays still use the lunar calendar socially
laws.sourceLabel: Act on the Enforcement of Age Counting Method 2023 — Ministry of Government Legislation

quiz.q: What change took effect in South Korea on 28 June 2023 regarding age?
options: International age (full years lived) became the administrative standard
Lunar calendar became the only recognised system
quiz.explanation: On 28 June 2023, the Act on the Enforcement of Age Counting Method made international age (full years lived) the standard for administrative and contractual purposes — replacing the old ‘Korean Age’ system.

laws.title: Yoon Suk-yeol's Martial Law Declaration — South Korea's December 2024 Constitutional Crisis
laws.subtitle: President Yoon declared emergency martial law December 3, 2024; National Assembly voted to lift it within hours
laws.fullDescription: On December 3, 2024, South Korean President Yoon Suk-yeol made a stunning announcement: declaring emergency martial law for the first time since 1980, citing 'anti-state forces' in the opposition. Armed soldiers entered the National Assembly building. However, the National Assembly — South Korea's parliament — mobilized within hours: 190 members voted to lift martial law at 1am December 4, 2024, defeating the declaration through the constitutional mechanism requiring a majority vote to end martial law. Yoon lifted martial law 6 hours after declaring it. The Constitutional Court suspended Yoon from presidential powers after impeachment on December 14. South Korea's democratic institutions — National Assembly procedures, military commanders who refused to block the parliamentary vote, and public protest — proved resilient. Yoon was arrested in January 2025.
laws.penalty: The National Assembly's December 4 vote to lift martial law was constitutionally binding. Yoon was impeached December 14; his presidential powers were suspended pending Constitutional Court review. Criminal charges for insurrection followed.
exceptions: The episode is recent history and formal legal outcomes were still unfolding as of early 2025
Constitutional Court review was the formal mechanism to determine Yoon's ultimate fate
Military commanders who refused to enforce martial law unconstitutionally were not prosecuted
laws.sourceLabel: BBC News — South Korea Martial Law Crisis December 2024

quiz.q: How long did South Korean President Yoon Suk-yeol's December 2024 martial law declaration last?
quiz.explanation: Yoon Suk-yeol's emergency martial law declaration lasted approximately 6 hours — from its announcement on December 3, 2024, until the National Assembly voted 190-0 to lift it at approximately 1am on December 4. This rapid reversal demonstrated the strength of South Korea's constitutional mechanisms for checking executive overreach.

laws.title: Yoon Suk-yeol Martial Law Decree
laws.subtitle: President's six-hour martial law declaration triggered impeachment and constitutional crisis
laws.fullDescription: On December 3, 2024, South Korean President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law — the first in 44 years — citing 'anti-state forces' in the opposition-controlled National Assembly. Armed troops surrounded parliament but were physically blocked by citizens and lawmakers. The National Assembly voted 190-0 to lift martial law; Yoon rescinded the order within six hours. The crisis triggered impeachment proceedings: the National Assembly impeached Yoon on December 14, 2024, suspending his powers. Acting President Han Duck-soo assumed duties. The Constitutional Court began deliberations on whether to permanently remove Yoon from office.
laws.penalty: Unconstitutional declaration of martial law is a criminal offense under South Korean law. Yoon was arrested January 2025 for insurrection — the first sitting or former president arrested while under criminal investigation.
exceptions: National Assembly has constitutional authority to lift martial law by majority vote
Constitutional Court has 180 days to rule on impeachment
Prime Minister automatically becomes acting president during presidential suspension
laws.sourceLabel: Hankyoreh — South Korea Martial Law Crisis

quiz.q: How did South Korea's National Assembly respond to President Yoon's 2024 martial law declaration?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's National Assembly voted 190-0 to lift President Yoon's martial law declaration within hours of it being issued, exercising their constitutional authority — leading to the order being rescinded after just six hours.

laws.title: BTS Military Service Exemption Debate
laws.subtitle: South Korea's mandatory conscription law denied K-pop superstars an exemption — they served anyway
laws.fullDescription: South Korea requires all able-bodied men to serve 18–21 months in the military — one of the world's strictest conscription systems, maintained because of the ongoing North Korean threat. Classical musicians and Olympic athletes receive exemptions, but K-pop stars historically did not. BTS, South Korea's most economically valuable cultural export (contributing an estimated $5 billion annually), sparked years of national debate about whether they deserved an exemption for their cultural impact. In 2022, parliament passed a narrow amendment allowing delays (not exemptions) for top cultural figures up to age 30. BTS members began enlisting from 2023, finishing service by 2025.
laws.penalty: Draft evasion: up to 3 years imprisonment and a criminal record. 'Yellow envelope' (anonymous draft evasion reporting system): neighbors can report evasion. Conscientious objection was criminalized until 2019 — now alternative service (36 months) is permitted.
exceptions: Jehovah's Witnesses and other conscientious objectors may perform alternative service since 2020
Top classical and traditional music performers receive full exemptions
BTS received delay provisions but not full exemptions like Olympic gold medalists
laws.sourceLabel: Military Manpower Administration — Republic of Korea

quiz.q: What type of accommodation did South Korea create for BTS members regarding military service?
options: A full exemption equivalent to Olympic athletes
A permanent exemption from all military duties
A delay provision allowing them to postpone enlistment until age 30
quiz.explanation: South Korea's 2022 amendment created a delay provision — not an exemption — allowing top cultural figures like BTS members to postpone military enlistment until age 30. BTS members subsequently enlisted for full 18-month service from 2023 onwards.

laws.title: Hallyu — Korean Wave Cultural Export Policy
laws.subtitle: South Korea turned K-pop, K-drama, and K-beauty into a $10 billion+ cultural export industry
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's 'Korean Wave' (Hallyu) — encompassing K-pop, K-dramas, K-films, and K-beauty — is a deliberate government-supported cultural export strategy. After the 1997 financial crisis, the government invested heavily in cultural industries: the Culture Industry Promotion Act (1999) created the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA) to fund entertainment production and exports. BTS generated an estimated $5 billion annual economic impact; Parasite (Academy Award Best Picture 2020) and Squid Game (Netflix's most-watched series) demonstrated global reach. Korea earns $12+ billion annually from cultural exports, with young consumers in 100+ countries adopting Korean fashion, food, and language.
laws.penalty: Copyright infringement of K-pop or K-drama content: civil and criminal liability under the Copyright Act. Unauthorized fan merchandise: trademark infringement. Cultural content that violates broadcasting standards: KOCCA sanctions.
exceptions: Fan-created content (fanfiction, covers) has customary tolerance from entertainment companies
Educational use of K-pop for Korean language learning receives informal blessing
Government-funded content is available for educational redistribution

quiz.q: Which South Korean film made history by winning the Academy Award for Best Picture in 2020?
quiz.explanation: Bong Joon-ho's Parasite won the Academy Award for Best Picture in 2020 — becoming the first non-English language film to win the award and representing a milestone for South Korea's Hallyu cultural wave alongside the global dominance of K-pop and K-dramas.

laws.title: AI Basic Act: South Korea's Foundational AI Governance Law
laws.subtitle: South Korea became one of the first countries to pass comprehensive AI regulation in 2024
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Artificial Intelligence Basic Act (passed December 2024, effective January 2026) establishes a national framework for AI governance. It classifies AI systems into 'high-impact' categories — including AI used in healthcare, transportation, elections, and critical infrastructure — requiring risk assessment, transparency obligations, and liability frameworks. The law creates the AI Safety Institute and requires AI developers to label AI-generated content. South Korea was among the world's first nations to pass standalone comprehensive AI legislation, alongside the EU AI Act. Seoul is home to Samsung, SK Hynix, and LG, giving South Korea significant stakes in the global AI regulatory race.
laws.penalty: Deploying non-compliant high-impact AI: fines up to KRW 30 million (~$22,000) and corrective orders. Failure to label AI-generated content: separate administrative penalties
exceptions: AI used for national defense and security has a separate classified framework
Small developers with fewer than 10 employees have reduced obligations during a transition period
laws.sourceLabel: South Korea Ministry of Science and ICT

quiz.q: When did South Korea's AI Basic Act take effect?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's AI Basic Act was passed in December 2024 and took effect in January 2026, making South Korea one of the first countries globally to implement comprehensive standalone AI legislation.

laws.title: Yoon Suk-yeol's Martial Law & Impeachment: South Korea's Democratic Test
laws.subtitle: South Korea's president declared martial law for 6 hours in December 2024 — was impeached, removed, and arrested in a rapid constitutional sequence
laws.fullDescription: On December 3, 2024, President Yoon Suk-yeol declared emergency martial law, claiming the National Assembly was 'anti-state.' Soldiers surrounded parliament; the interior minister tried to arrest opposition leaders. But 190 National Assembly members rushed to the chamber and voted 190-0 to lift martial law within 6 hours — the required majority was 151. Yoon reversed the declaration but was impeached by the National Assembly on December 14. The Constitutional Court upheld the impeachment and removed him from office on April 4, 2025. He was arrested on insurrection charges — carrying up to life imprisonment or the death penalty. Acting presidents served in the interim. South Korea's democratic institutions held against an executive assault.
laws.penalty: Insurrection (Yoon's charge): life imprisonment or death penalty under Korean law. Military officers who participated: criminal prosecution for mutiny
exceptions: The Constitutional Court's removal vote required 6 of 8 justices — it passed 8-0
South Korea has previously impeached a president: Park Geun-hye was removed in 2017 for corruption

quiz.q: How many hours did Yoon Suk-yeol's emergency martial law last before the National Assembly voted to lift it?
quiz.explanation: Yoon Suk-yeol's emergency martial law lasted approximately 6 hours — from its declaration late on December 3, 2024 to the National Assembly's 190-0 vote to lift it at around 1 a.m. on December 4, demonstrating the resilience of South Korea's democratic institutions.

laws.title: Shutdown Law (Cinderella Law)
laws.subtitle: South Korea's Shutdown Law banned under-16s from gaming after midnight
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's 'Shutdown Law' (Youth Protection Act amendment, 2011) banned minors under 16 from accessing online games between midnight and 6am to combat gaming addiction — nicknamed the 'Cinderella Law.' Game companies had to verify ages and implement automatic logout systems. At its peak, Korea had some of the world's most competitive professional gaming cultures and highest gaming addiction rates. The law was repealed in 2021, replaced by an 'opt-in' system where parents can choose to restrict gaming hours. South Korea became the first country to officially classify 'internet gaming disorder' as a clinical diagnosis and established gaming addiction treatment centers.
laws.penalty: Game companies that failed to enforce the shutdown faced fines; under the new opt-in system, violations of parental restrictions are handled by the platforms
exceptions: Educational and non-entertainment games were exempt
The opt-in replacement system is voluntary for parents
laws.sourceLabel: Korea Ministry of Gender Equality and Family

quiz.q: What nickname was given to South Korea's law banning under-16s from gaming after midnight?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's gaming curfew was nicknamed the 'Cinderella Law' because — like Cinderella's midnight curfew — it forced young gamers off their computers at midnight. It was repealed in 2021.

laws.title: Constitutional Court Impeachment Power
laws.subtitle: South Korea's Constitutional Court removed two presidents through impeachment
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Constitutional Court Act (1988) gives the court exclusive power to rule on presidential impeachment votes passed by the National Assembly. The court's jurisdiction has been exercised twice: Park Geun-hye (2017) — the court unanimously upheld her impeachment after massive 'Candlelight Revolution' protests over corruption and abuse of power, making her the first Korean president removed by impeachment. Yoon Suk-yeol (2025) — the court upheld his impeachment following his short-lived declaration of martial law in December 2024. Both decisions demonstrated that South Korea's democracy could hold powerful leaders accountable.
laws.penalty: Impeached and removed presidents lose the office but retain certain security and pension benefits (reduced); criminal prosecution proceeds separately
exceptions: The Constitutional Court ruling on impeachment is final and not subject to appeal
Presidents can only be impeached by a two-thirds National Assembly majority

quiz.q: Which Korean president was removed by the Constitutional Court in 2025 after declaring martial law?
quiz.explanation: Yoon Suk-yeol was impeached by South Korea's National Assembly in December 2024 after briefly declaring martial law, and removed from office by the Constitutional Court in 2025 — the second South Korean president removed by impeachment.

laws.title: Smart City Digital Infrastructure Regulations
laws.subtitle: Seoul's Digital Master Plan governs AI, data, and urban technology deployment
laws.fullDescription: Seoul is recognized as one of the world's most advanced smart cities, and its Digital Seoul Master Plan 2030 (updated 2022) governs how artificial intelligence, big data, IoT sensors, and digital twins are deployed in urban management. The plan includes regulations on public surveillance cameras (subject to personal information protection law), autonomous vehicle testing zones, digital welfare services, and open government data APIs. Seoul's Personal Information Protection Act (aligned with the national law) requires explicit consent for data collection and mandates data minimization. The city also operates a 'metaverse Seoul' platform and has pioneered blockchain-based resident services. The Digital New Deal legislation at the national level funds much of this infrastructure while establishing cybersecurity requirements for smart city operators.
laws.penalty: Violations of the Personal Information Protection Act carry fines up to 300 million KRW; smart city operators face license revocation for cybersecurity breaches
exceptions: Emergency services may access data without prior consent in life-threatening situations
Government agencies have broader data access rights under national security provisions

laws.title: 2024 Martial Law Crisis and Constitutional Confrontation
laws.subtitle: President Yoon Suk-yeol's brief December 2024 martial law declaration triggered his impeachment
laws.fullDescription: South Korea experienced its most severe constitutional crisis since democratization when President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law on December 3, 2024, citing 'anti-state forces' in the opposition. The martial law declaration — which would have suspended the National Assembly and imposed military rule — was extraordinary: the National Assembly convened within hours (despite troops surrounding it) and voted 190-0 to overturn the martial law declaration, as required by Article 77 of the Constitution. Yoon lifted the declaration within 6 hours. The National Assembly then passed two impeachment motions; the Constitutional Court upheld his removal in April 2025. It was South Korea's second presidential impeachment (after Park Geun-hye in 2017). The crisis demonstrated both the strength of South Korea's democratic institutions (the Assembly successfully overturned martial law within hours) and the fragility of constitutional norms when leaders test them.
laws.penalty: Martial law declared in violation of constitutional procedures: criminal prosecution for insurrection (which carries the death penalty in South Korea); impeachment removes the president from office
exceptions: Constitutional martial law during actual war or comparable emergency is permitted under Article 77
Military commanders have legal duties to follow martial law orders until legally overturned
The Constitutional Court has exclusive jurisdiction over presidential impeachment

laws.title: Korean Wave (Hallyu) and Cultural Content Export Promotion Law
laws.subtitle: South Korea's legal framework promotes K-pop, K-drama, and cultural exports as strategic economic assets
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's 'Korean Wave' (Hallyu) — the global spread of Korean popular culture including K-pop, K-drama, Korean film, food, and beauty — has been supported by deliberate government policy and legal frameworks. The Content Industry Promotion Act (2010, regularly amended) designates cultural content as a strategic export industry and provides government funding, tax incentives, and export promotion through the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA). The Hallyu Economic Effect: K-pop exports exceeded $1.2 billion in 2023; Korean beauty (K-beauty) exports exceeded $8 billion; Korean food exports grew to $10 billion annually; and Korean cultural exports overall contributed significantly to the 'Korea Premium' in tourism and consumer goods. South Korea's copyright law protects musical works, choreography (critically important for K-pop), and broadcasting rights. Fan culture platforms and streaming services are governed by the E-Commerce and Digital Transactions Act. BTS-related intellectual property management and HYBE's legal disputes over artist contracts attracted global attention.
laws.penalty: Copyright infringement of K-pop content: civil damages plus criminal penalties up to 5 years; unauthorized performance of choreography: civil claims; 'sajaegi' (chart manipulation by bulk purchasing): investigated by police and industry associations
exceptions: Fan-created content (fan fiction, covers) has a traditionally tolerated zone in Korea
Academic analysis of Hallyu has broad fair use protection
Not-for-profit cultural exchange events have reduced copyright requirements

laws.title: President Yoon's Martial Law Declaration and Impeachment
laws.subtitle: South Korea's president briefly declared martial law; was impeached within days
laws.fullDescription: On December 3, 2024, President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law in South Korea — citing anti-state forces and parliamentary obstruction — for the first time since 1980. The National Assembly voted 190-0 to lift martial law within hours. Yoon rescinded it at dawn. The National Assembly impeached Yoon on December 14, 2024, with 204 votes including members of his own party. Acting presidents Han Duck-soo and then Choi Sang-mok governed while the Constitutional Court reviewed the impeachment. The case involved Article 77 of the Constitution (martial law) and Article 65 (impeachment) — South Korea's constitutional crisis captured global attention.
laws.penalty: Martial law violations: civilian courts retain jurisdiction once martial law is lifted. Unconstitutional martial law declaration: impeachment and potential criminal prosecution.
exceptions: National Assembly has power to lift martial law by majority vote — this constitutional check worked
Criminal courts resume jurisdiction as soon as martial law is rescinded

quiz.q: How quickly did South Korea's National Assembly respond to Yoon's 2024 martial law declaration?
options: Within hours, voting 190-0 to lift it
It took 3 days to convene an emergency session
The Supreme Court blocked it before the Assembly could vote
It took a week — Yoon withdrew it voluntarily
quiz.explanation: The National Assembly convened within hours of Yoon's martial law declaration and voted 190-0 to lift it, forcing Yoon to rescind the order at dawn — a remarkable demonstration of constitutional checks functioning under pressure.

laws.title: South Korea's Population Crisis and Pronatalist Policies
laws.subtitle: South Korea has the world's lowest birth rate; the government offers massive financial incentives
laws.fullDescription: South Korea has the world's lowest fertility rate — approximately 0.72 in 2023 (compared to the 2.1 replacement rate). Seoul's fertility rate dropped to an unprecedented 0.55. The government has spent over $200 billion on pronatalist policies since 2006 with minimal effect. Measures include cash payments (up to ₩2 million at birth, increasing), extended parental leave, subsidized childcare, and housing preferences for families. President Yoon (before his impeachment) declared the situation a 'national emergency.' Deep-rooted causes include extreme education costs, housing unaffordability, long work culture, and women's rejection of traditional gender roles. South Korea's population began shrinking in 2020 and could halve by 2100.
laws.penalty: Employers denying legally mandated parental leave: fines up to ₩5 million per violation. Workplace discrimination against pregnant women: civil and criminal penalties.
exceptions: Self-employed workers have access to voluntary parental leave contribution schemes
Adoptive parents entitled to same parental leave as biological parents
laws.sourceLabel: Korean Ministry of Health and Welfare

quiz.q: What was South Korea's total fertility rate in 2023, and why is it alarming?
options: 1.4 — below replacement but comparable to other developed nations
0.72 — the world's lowest, far below the 2.1 replacement rate needed to maintain population
0.5 — lower than any country has ever recorded in peacetime
quiz.explanation: South Korea's 2023 fertility rate of approximately 0.72 was the world's lowest — less than a third of the 2.1 replacement rate — meaning South Korea's population faces dramatic shrinkage within decades without significant immigration.

laws.title: South Korean Platform Accountability Act
laws.subtitle: Large platforms face strict content moderation and algorithm disclosure rules
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Platform Accountability Act (2023) requires major online platforms to establish transparent content moderation policies, provide explanations for content removal or account restrictions, and submit annual reports on algorithmic systems to the Korea Communications Commission (KCC). Platforms must allow users to appeal moderation decisions within 24 hours. South Korea also has a strong real-name verification system for online services. The law positions South Korea as a global leader in platform regulation alongside the EU's DSA.
laws.penalty: Failure to establish complaint resolution mechanism: fines up to KRW 100 million (~$75,000). Failure to submit algorithm reports: fines up to KRW 30 million. Repeat violations can result in temporary service suspension orders
exceptions: Platforms under 10 million Korean monthly users have lighter requirements
News media platforms have separate press freedom protections
Government-operated platforms exempt from commercial platform rules

quiz.q: What must South Korean platforms do when they remove content or restrict an account?
options: Provide an explanation and allow appeals within 24 hours
quiz.explanation: South Korea's Platform Accountability Act requires platforms to explain content removal decisions and process user appeals within 24 hours.

laws.title: South Korea's December 2024 Martial Law Crisis
laws.subtitle: President Yoon declared brief martial law, was impeached
laws.fullDescription: South Korean President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law on December 3, 2024 — the first since 1980 — citing opposition 'anti-state forces.' The National Assembly voted to lift it within hours (the Constitution requires National Assembly approval to maintain martial law). Yoon was subsequently impeached by the National Assembly on December 14, 2024 with bipartisan support. The Constitutional Court upheld his removal from office in April 2025. Yoon was arrested on insurrection charges — the most serious criminal charge in South Korean law. Acting presidents managed the government through the crisis.
laws.penalty: Insurrection: up to life imprisonment or death penalty under South Korea's criminal code — the most serious charges possible. Martial law abuse: criminal prosecution. Military commanders who participated: court-martial. Officials who aided unlawful martial law: up to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Members of National Assembly who voted to lift martial law were constitutionally protected in their parliamentary role
Constitutional Court justices have immunity for their rulings
Diplomatic personnel had normal immunity throughout

quiz.q: How quickly did South Korea's National Assembly vote to lift Yoon's December 2024 martial law declaration?
options: It was not lifted — it lasted 1 month
quiz.explanation: South Korea's National Assembly voted to lift President Yoon's martial law declaration within hours of it being announced — exercising their constitutional power to nullify it, leading ultimately to Yoon's impeachment and criminal prosecution for insurrection.

laws.title: South Korea's AI Industry Promotion Act
laws.subtitle: Korea supports AI development while implementing safety frameworks
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Artificial Intelligence Industry Promotion Act (enacted 2024) establishes a framework for AI industry support and basic safety requirements. Unlike the EU's prescriptive AI Act, South Korea's approach balances promoting innovation with addressing high-risk AI. The act requires impact assessments for high-risk AI systems in healthcare, employment, education, and public services. The Korea Communications Commission and the Ministry of Science and ICT share AI oversight. South Korea has major AI investments from Samsung, LG, Kakao, Naver, and SK Telecom. The law also establishes an AI Safety Institute.
laws.penalty: High-risk AI deployment without impact assessment: fines up to KRW 30 million. AI-generated deepfake sexual content: up to 5 years (separate law). Election deepfakes: up to 7 years. AI manipulation of financial markets: existing securities law applies
exceptions: R&D environments have lighter requirements during development phase
Military AI systems have separate defense ministry regulations
AI used in creative arts (music, film) has lighter oversight if clearly labeled
laws.sourceLabel: Korean Ministry of Science and ICT

quiz.q: How does South Korea's AI regulation approach differ from the EU's AI Act?
options: South Korea banned all AI entirely
South Korea's approach balances promotion with safety rather than being as prescriptive as the EU
South Korea has stricter rules than the EU on all AI
South Korea only regulates AI from foreign companies
quiz.explanation: South Korea's AI Act takes a more balanced approach between innovation promotion and safety oversight — establishing impact assessments for high-risk AI and an AI Safety Institute while avoiding the EU AI Act's more prescriptive prohibitions and mandatory requirements.

laws.title: Platform Power Restriction and App Store Antitrust Law
laws.subtitle: South Korea became the first country to ban app store monopolies
laws.fullDescription: South Korea made global history in 2021 by amending the Telecommunications Business Act to prohibit major app store operators (Apple and Google) from requiring developers to use their payment systems exclusively. This was the world's first law breaking app store payment monopolies. The Korea Communications Commission (KCC) can fine companies up to 3% of their South Korean revenue for violations. By 2024, both Apple and Google had complied under threat of fines, allowing alternative payment methods in South Korean versions of their apps. The law is closely watched globally as a model for similar legislation.
laws.penalty: Violation of app store payment monopoly ban: fines up to 3% of South Korean revenue; repeat violations: enhanced penalties
exceptions: Small app store platforms below threshold user numbers
Enterprise-only internal app distribution

quiz.q: What global first did South Korea achieve with its 2021 Telecommunications Business Act amendment?
options: First country to ban social media
First to require local data storage
First country to ban app store payment monopolies
quiz.explanation: South Korea became the first country in the world to legally prohibit app store operators from requiring exclusive use of their payment systems, breaking Apple and Google's payment monopolies.

laws.title: Martial Law Declaration and Constitutional Crisis 2024
laws.subtitle: South Korea's president briefly declared martial law in December 2024
laws.fullDescription: In December 2024, South Korean President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law — the first in over 40 years — citing threats from 'anti-state forces.' The National Assembly voted to lift the martial law within hours under the constitutional provision requiring parliamentary repeal. Yoon subsequently faced impeachment by the National Assembly, impeachment was upheld by the Constitutional Court, and he was removed from office. He faced criminal charges for insurrection. The events tested South Korea's constitutional democratic framework but ultimately demonstrated the resilience of its parliamentary checks on executive power.
laws.penalty: Insurrection by a sitting president: potential life imprisonment or death penalty; participating in unconstitutional martial law: up to life imprisonment
exceptions: Constitutional martial law declared under legitimate wartime conditions follows separate procedures
Actions by legislators under constitutional mandate to repeal martial law protected

quiz.q: How quickly did South Korea's National Assembly respond to President Yoon's 2024 martial law declaration?
options: Within hours — voted to lift it under constitutional authority
quiz.explanation: South Korea's National Assembly voted to lift President Yoon's December 2024 martial law declaration within hours, exercising its constitutional authority to repeal martial law — demonstrating the strength of South Korea's democratic checks.

laws.title: Personal Information Protection Act Amendments
laws.subtitle: South Korea strengthened its data protection law to align with global standards
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) was significantly amended in 2023 and 2024 to strengthen data subject rights, enhance privacy protections, and improve international alignment. The Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) gained enhanced enforcement powers including investigation authority over public agencies. Transfer of personal data overseas requires adequate protection verification. Pseudonymized data can be processed for statistical and research purposes without consent under specific conditions. Administrative fines were increased significantly. South Korea's privacy law is now considered one of the strongest in Asia, rivaling GDPR in scope.
laws.penalty: Serious PIPA violations: fines up to 3% of total revenue; unlawful overseas transfer of personal data: criminal penalties
exceptions: Journalistic, academic, and statistical purposes with appropriate safeguards
Emergency situations requiring processing to protect life or property

quiz.q: What government body gained enhanced enforcement powers under South Korea's amended PIPA?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) gained enhanced enforcement powers under the amended PIPA, including investigation authority over public agencies — making it a more independent and powerful privacy regulator.

laws.title: South Korea Yoon Impeachment and Constitutional Order
laws.subtitle: South Korea upholds democratic checks after attempted martial law
laws.fullDescription: In December 2024, President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law for approximately six hours before the National Assembly voted to reject it, forcing its immediate reversal. The Constitutional Court subsequently upheld Yoon's impeachment in April 2025. The episode demonstrated the resilience of South Korea's constitutional mechanisms. Legal reforms followed to clarify the conditions under which a president may declare martial law and to strengthen legislative checks on emergency powers.
laws.penalty: Presidential impeachment and removal from office; criminal investigation for insurrection charges; official accomplices face prosecution
exceptions: Legitimate emergency declarations approved by the National Assembly
National defense measures under separate Military Service Act
Presidential pardons for specific cases

quiz.q: How long did President Yoon's December 2024 martial law declaration last before being reversed?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's National Assembly voted to reject President Yoon's martial law declaration within approximately 6 hours, and the Constitutional Court later upheld his impeachment.

laws.title: South Korea Platform Competition Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea regulates dominant app stores and digital platforms
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted the Telecommunications Business Act amendment in 2021, the first law in the world to prohibit major app store operators (Apple, Google) from forcing developers to use their proprietary payment systems. South Korea's Korea Communications Commission enforces the law. The law also created obligations for large online platforms to provide interoperability and prohibits self-preferencing. South Korea has positioned itself as a global leader in digital market regulation, ahead of the EU's Digital Markets Act.
laws.penalty: Fines up to 3% of revenue for violations; corrective orders; repeat violations lead to increased penalties
exceptions: Small app store operators below market share thresholds
B2B software distribution platforms
Government app stores

quiz.q: What payment system restriction did South Korea become the first country to prohibit in 2021?
options: Credit card fees on digital purchases
App stores forcing developers to use their proprietary payment systems
quiz.explanation: South Korea's 2021 Telecommunications Business Act amendment was the first law in the world to prohibit major app stores (Apple App Store and Google Play) from requiring developers to use their own payment systems exclusively.

laws.title: South Korea Game Addiction and Youth Protection Laws
laws.subtitle: South Korea regulates online gaming to protect youth mental health
laws.fullDescription: South Korea has been a global pioneer in regulating video game addiction. The Shutdown Law (2011-2021) banned minors from online gaming between midnight and 6am. After the shutdown law was repealed in 2021 as paternalistic, South Korea replaced it with a game time selection system where parents can voluntarily set gaming hour limits for children. New regulations also require game companies to disclose loot box probability rates and limit purchases. The PC bang (gaming cafe) industry also faces youth protection rules.
laws.penalty: Game companies that fail to implement parental controls: fines; inadequate loot box probability disclosure: administrative penalties
exceptions: Single-player games without online connectivity
Educational games
Games rated for adults without youth-targeted features

quiz.q: What did South Korea replace its midnight gaming shutdown law with in 2021?
options: A complete ban on youth gaming
A voluntary parental game time selection system
quiz.explanation: South Korea replaced the Shutdown Law (mandatory midnight gaming ban for minors) with a voluntary system where parents can choose to set gaming hour limits for their children, shifting from mandatory restriction to parental choice.

laws.title: Online Platform Competition Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's rules preventing tech platform self-preferencing
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted the Online Platform Competition Promotion Act targeting large digital platforms designated as having market dominance. Designated platforms are prohibited from self-preferencing their own services over competitors in rankings and recommendations, engaging in tied selling that forces users to adopt related services, and using data collected from business users to compete against them. The Korea Fair Trade Commission can designate platforms as dominant and impose advance measures before completing full investigations.
laws.penalty: Violations by designated dominant platforms carry fines of up to 3% of relevant revenue; interim measures can be ordered immediately pending investigation
exceptions: Platforms below market share and revenue thresholds not designated as dominant
New entrants have 12-month grace period after reaching thresholds
Technical integration that demonstrably benefits consumers may be permitted

quiz.q: What anti-competitive practice does South Korea's platform competition act specifically prohibit dominant platforms from doing?
options: Charging different prices in different regions
Self-preferencing their own services in search rankings and recommendations
quiz.explanation: South Korea's Online Platform Competition Act specifically prohibits designated dominant platforms from self-preferencing their own products and services in rankings and recommendations over competitor offerings.

laws.title: Martial Law Attempt and Constitutional Crisis
laws.subtitle: South Korea's short-lived martial law declaration and its legal aftermath
laws.fullDescription: South Korea experienced a constitutional crisis when President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law in December 2024 for approximately 6 hours before parliament voted to lift it. The National Assembly physically blocked military personnel from entering the parliament building and voted 190-0 to reject the martial law declaration, as required by the constitution. President Yoon was subsequently impeached by the National Assembly and arrested on insurrection charges. The Constitutional Court upheld the impeachment. The events highlighted South Korea's constitutional safeguards against authoritarian backsliding.
laws.penalty: Insurrection carries the death penalty or life imprisonment under South Korean law; the former president was charged with insurrection for the martial law declaration; military officers who participated faced separate charges
exceptions: Military personnel who refused or withdrew comply with their constitutional duty
Parliamentary members exercising their constitutional vote are protected
Civil servants who followed lawful orders during the brief period have mitigated liability

quiz.q: How did South Korea's National Assembly respond to President Yoon's December 2024 martial law declaration?
options: They endorsed the martial law declaration
They were unable to meet due to military blockade
They voted 190-0 to reject the martial law declaration within hours
They waited to see how citizens responded before acting
quiz.explanation: The South Korean National Assembly voted 190-0 to reject President Yoon's martial law declaration within approximately 6 hours, with members physically entering the parliament building despite attempts to block them, successfully invoking their constitutional power to lift martial law.

laws.title: AI and Deep Fake Regulation Laws
laws.subtitle: South Korea's laws targeting AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted laws specifically targeting AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery (deepfakes), following widespread harm particularly to women and girls. The law criminalized creating, distributing, and possessing such material without consent, with significant prison sentences. South Korea had a major public awareness campaign after it was revealed that Telegram groups were being used to share deepfake pornography targeting real women including teachers. Police created specialized units to investigate these crimes. The laws were part of a broader crackdown on digital sexual crimes.
laws.penalty: Creating deepfake intimate imagery without consent carries up to 5 years imprisonment; distributing such content carries up to 7 years; possession for distribution carries up to 3 years
exceptions: Consensual adult content with participants' documented consent is not covered
Art and satire that does not create sexual content are protected
Academic research on detection technology has modified requirements

quiz.q: What platform was revealed to be hosting deepfake pornography groups in South Korea, prompting tougher legislation?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's deepfake legislation was partly prompted by revelations that Telegram groups were being used to share AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery targeting real women including teachers — sparking national outrage and accelerating legislation to criminalize deepfake sexual content.

laws.title: South Korea Martial Law Declaration and Constitutional Crisis
laws.subtitle: President Yoon's short-lived martial law declaration and impeachment
laws.fullDescription: South Korean President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law on December 3, 2024, citing 'anti-state forces,' in the first such declaration since 1980. The National Assembly voted 190-0 within six hours to lift the martial law, as required by the constitution when a majority of members demand its lifting. Yoon's martial law was rescinded within hours, but he was impeached by the National Assembly on December 14, 2024. The Constitutional Court upheld his removal in April 2025.
laws.penalty: Under the Military Criminal Act and Constitution, unauthorized or politically motivated martial law declarations are subject to criminal prosecution. Yoon faced charges of insurrection, carrying potential life imprisonment or death penalty under Korean law.
exceptions: Constitutional martial law during genuine national security emergencies remains lawful under Article 77
Military commanders operating under lawful orders during valid martial law retain legal protection

quiz.q: How did South Korea's National Assembly respond to President Yoon's 2024 martial law declaration?
options: It was deadlocked and took no action
It voted 190-0 to lift the martial law
It referred the matter to the Constitutional Court
quiz.explanation: South Korea's National Assembly voted 190-0 within six hours to lift President Yoon's martial law declaration, exercising its constitutional power to override the president, after which Yoon rescinded the order and was subsequently impeached.

laws.title: South Korea Constitutional Court Upholds Yoon Removal
laws.subtitle: April 2025 ruling confirming presidential impeachment
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Constitutional Court issued its unanimous ruling in April 2025, upholding the National Assembly's impeachment of President Yoon Suk-yeol and permanently removing him from office. The court found his December 2024 martial law declaration was unconstitutional and amounted to insurrection. Acting President Han Duck-soo had served for months while the case was deliberated. A new presidential election was required within 60 days of the ruling, with Lee Jae-myung of the opposition Democratic Party emerging as the frontrunner.
laws.penalty: Yoon faces criminal trial for insurrection under the Military Criminal Act — an offense that carries the death penalty or life imprisonment in the most serious cases, though prosecutors typically seek lesser sentences in politically sensitive cases.
exceptions: Former presidents who cooperate with investigations may request bail under general criminal procedure rules
Constitutional immunity does not apply to acts of insurrection under Korean constitutional jurisprudence

quiz.q: What vote standard did South Korea's Constitutional Court apply in upholding Yoon's removal?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's Constitutional Court issued a unanimous 8-0 ruling upholding President Yoon's removal, finding his martial law declaration unconstitutional. A unanimous ruling carries greater political legitimacy and foreclosed any argument that the removal was politically motivated.

laws.title: South Korea Social Media Youth Protection Law
laws.subtitle: Under-14 restrictions and parental monitoring requirements
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted youth protection legislation for online platforms in 2024, requiring parental consent for children under 14 to use social media platforms, mandating platforms to provide parents with monitoring tools, restricting nighttime access for minors (late-night lockout features for under-18s), and requiring platforms to proactively reduce addictive features in products marketed to youth. South Korea had existing internet gaming night-time restrictions ('Cinderella Law') that had been partially relaxed.
laws.penalty: Platforms that fail to implement parental consent mechanisms for under-14 users: fines up to KRW 3 billion. Platforms that knowingly allow addictive design features targeting minors: fines up to 3% of South Korean revenue.
exceptions: Educational platforms with teacher-controlled access exempt from parental consent requirements
Emergency communication features retained even during nighttime lockout periods
Platforms with verified under 10,000 South Korean monthly users subject to simplified compliance

quiz.q: What was the earlier South Korean internet restriction known as the 'Cinderella Law'?
options: A ban on internet use for minors on school nights
Late-night online gaming restrictions for minors
A requirement for parental supervision of all online activity
Content filtering for violent video games
quiz.explanation: South Korea's 'Cinderella Law' restricted online gaming access for minors during late-night hours — requiring gaming platforms to block under-16 users from midnight to 6am. It was partially relaxed in 2021 after effectiveness concerns, with the 2024 law taking a broader approach to youth social media protection.

laws.title: Yoon Suk-yeol Martial Law Declaration and Reversal
laws.subtitle: Presidential martial law declared and reversed within 6 hours
laws.fullDescription: President Yoon Suk-yeol declared emergency martial law citing anti-state forces in opposition, deploying troops to the National Assembly. The National Assembly voted to lift martial law within 6 hours, and the declaration was reversed. Yoon was subsequently impeached by the National Assembly, arrested, and faced criminal charges of insurrection — the first sitting president arrested in South Korean history.
laws.penalty: The president faced impeachment, suspension of powers, and criminal insurrection charges carrying up to life imprisonment or death penalty
exceptions: Parliamentary staff and citizens who entered the National Assembly during the martial law were not prosecuted

quiz.q: How long did President Yoon's martial law declaration last before the National Assembly voted to lift it?
quiz.explanation: President Yoon's martial law declaration lasted approximately 6 hours before the National Assembly convened an emergency session and voted to lift it, forcing the president to reverse the declaration.

laws.title: K-Content and Korean Wave Export Support Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea legally supports hallyu cultural exports globally
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted legislation establishing the Korea Culture and Content Agency with expanded powers and budget to support Korean Wave (hallyu) cultural exports including K-pop, K-drama, webtoons, and K-food. The law created export credit insurance for Korean entertainment companies, established a joint venture fund with major streaming platforms, and mandated Korean cultural content quotas on domestic platforms.
laws.penalty: Domestic streaming platforms failing to meet Korean content quotas: fines from KRW 10 million; fraudulent export subsidy claims: repayment plus criminal referral
exceptions: Very small independent streaming services with under 100,000 subscribers exempt from quota requirements
International co-productions with majority Korean creative control count at 150% toward quotas

quiz.q: What is the Korean term for the global Korean cultural wave that South Korea's export laws support?
quiz.explanation: Hallyu (한류), meaning 'Korean Wave,' refers to the global spread of South Korean culture including K-pop, K-drama, K-food, and other cultural exports that South Korea's laws now formally support and fund.

laws.title: K-Chip Act and Semiconductor R&D Tax Credits
laws.subtitle: South Korea's subsidies to keep Samsung and SK Hynix competitive
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted the K-Chip Act (Semiconductor Special Act), providing the world's largest semiconductor tax credits — up to 25% for large companies and 35% for SMEs — for chip manufacturing investment. The law also fast-tracked environmental permits for new fab construction, created a dedicated semiconductor industrial complex, and established a government-industry fund of $19 billion for R&D.
laws.penalty: Companies claiming tax credits without meeting actual investment milestones: clawback of full credit amount plus penalty
exceptions: Foreign companies investing in South Korea receive same credits as domestic firms
Joint ventures with universities receive enhanced R&D credit rates

quiz.q: What is the maximum semiconductor tax credit available to SMEs under South Korea's K-Chip Act?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's K-Chip Act provides SMEs (small and medium enterprises) in semiconductor manufacturing with tax credits of up to 35% on investment — higher than the 25% available to large companies — to encourage broader industry development.

laws.title: Korea Nuclear Policy Reversal and SMR Development
laws.subtitle: South Korea restores nuclear expansion after Green Party setback
laws.fullDescription: South Korea reversed a previous plan to phase out nuclear power, instead committing to expanding nuclear capacity to 35% of electricity by 2036. Legislation enabled new large reactor construction at existing nuclear sites, created a Small Modular Reactor (SMR) development programme, and exported nuclear technology agreements with UAE, Poland, and Egypt. Korea emerged as a major nuclear technology exporter.
laws.penalty: Nuclear operators failing regulatory safety checks: mandatory shutdown; SMR companies claiming R&D credits without meeting milestones: clawback
exceptions: Decommissioned older reactors not subject to restart under expansion law — only new construction
Safety critical maintenance allows exceptions to standard procurement timelines

quiz.q: What nuclear electricity share is South Korea targeting by 2036?
quiz.explanation: South Korea committed to expanding nuclear power to 35% of electricity generation by 2036 — reversing the previous government's phase-out policy — recognising nuclear as essential to both energy security and achieving clean energy goals.

laws.title: South Korea AI Chipset Leadership and Semiconductor Alliance Act
laws.subtitle: Samsung, SK Hynix and the global chip race
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted the Semiconductor AI Leadership and Alliance Act 2025, responding to intensifying competition from Taiwan, the US, and China in advanced chip manufacturing. The law provides KRW 26 trillion (approximately $20 billion) in tax credits and direct subsidies for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix's advanced DRAM, HBM (High Bandwidth Memory for AI applications), and NAND investments, establishes the Korea Semiconductor Alliance linking the major firms with universities for workforce development, mandates government investment in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment stockpiling, creates a supply chain resilience requirement mandating domestic capacity for at least 3 months of critical chip production, and establishes reciprocal investment partnerships with the US CHIPS Act ecosystem.
laws.penalty: Technology transfer to restricted entities: KRW 5 trillion fine plus 20 years imprisonment; chip design espionage: 25 years; supply chain resilience non-compliance: loss of subsidy eligibility
exceptions: Academic research partnerships with verified institutions have modified technology transfer framework
Legacy semiconductor processes above 28nm have simplified export controls
Emergency semiconductor supply agreements during global shortages reviewed case-by-case
laws.sourceLabel: Korean Ministry of Science and ICT

quiz.q: What type of memory chip, critical for AI applications, is South Korea's SK Hynix particularly dominant in producing?
quiz.explanation: SK Hynix is the world's leading producer of HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) — the specialized memory chips that sit directly on AI accelerator packages like Nvidia's H100/H200, making South Korea a critical node in the global AI supply chain.

laws.title: South Korea Constitutional Crisis and Presidential Impeachment
laws.subtitle: Martial law crisis and democratic resilience
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted the Constitutional Democracy Protection and Crisis Prevention Act 2025, following President Yoon Suk-yeol's extraordinary December 2024 declaration of martial law — reversed within 6 hours after the National Assembly voted to lift it — leading to his impeachment by the National Assembly and arrest. The law creates constitutional guardrails prohibiting future martial law declarations without National Assembly prior approval in all but active foreign invasion scenarios, establishes a Constitutional Emergency Protocol requiring Constitutional Court review within 24 hours of any emergency declaration, strengthens National Assembly's ability to convene emergency sessions without presidential permission, creates the Democracy Resilience Commission monitoring executive power concentration, and establishes transparency requirements for National Security Council deliberations.
laws.penalty: Unconstitutional martial law declaration: life imprisonment; obstruction of National Assembly emergency session: 20 years; presidential emergency power abuse: immediate impeachment trigger plus criminal prosecution
exceptions: Legitimate national security emergencies with foreign aggression retain emergency powers framework
Regional natural disaster emergency declarations governed under separate Disaster Response Law
Presidential executive orders in non-emergency contexts have separate legislative review

quiz.q: How long did President Yoon Suk-yeol's December 2024 martial law declaration last before the National Assembly voted to lift it?
quiz.explanation: President Yoon Suk-yeol's martial law declaration in December 2024 lasted only approximately 6 hours before the National Assembly convened an emergency session and voted to lift it — a remarkable demonstration of South Korea's democratic resilience and constitutional mechanisms.

laws.title: Presidential Martial Law Crisis and Constitutional Reform Act
laws.subtitle: Post-Yoon impeachment governance stabilization measures
laws.fullDescription: Following President Yoon Suk-yeol's shocking declaration of martial law in December 2024 and his subsequent impeachment, South Korea enacted sweeping constitutional and governance reforms to prevent future abuse of emergency powers. The legislation limits presidential authority to declare martial law, requires immediate National Assembly approval, and establishes new independent oversight of the military chain of command. It also reforms the impeachment process to ensure faster resolution of constitutional crises.
laws.penalty: Illegal declaration of martial law carries charges of insurrection, punishable by life imprisonment or death. Military officers who follow illegal orders to suppress the Assembly face criminal liability.
exceptions: Legitimate national security emergencies following a North Korean attack or natural disaster of catastrophic scale retain accelerated presidential emergency powers with parliamentary oversight

quiz.q: What extraordinary event in December 2024 triggered South Korea's constitutional reform?
options: President Yoon's declaration of martial law
quiz.explanation: President Yoon Suk-yeol's brief but shocking declaration of martial law in December 2024, followed by his impeachment, triggered major constitutional reforms to prevent future abuse of emergency powers.

laws.title: AI Industrial Policy and Semiconductor Sovereignty Act
laws.subtitle: Competing with US and China in strategic technology
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted comprehensive AI and semiconductor industrial policy legislation to maintain its position as a global chip manufacturing powerhouse amid the US-China technology war. The law provides substantial government subsidies for TSMC and Samsung fab expansions, creates an AI Safety Institute, establishes data governance standards for AI training, and implements export controls on advanced semiconductor technology aligned with US partner restrictions.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized export of controlled semiconductor technology to sanctioned countries carries up to 7 years imprisonment and fines up to 5 times the value of the export. Companies that accept semiconductor subsidies must maintain Korean employment levels for ten years.
exceptions: Academic semiconductor research has simplified export control procedures for non-military applications
Component suppliers to approved allied country manufacturers retain broader exemptions

quiz.q: Which South Korean company, alongside TSMC, is a global leader in advanced semiconductor manufacturing?
quiz.explanation: Samsung is South Korea's leading semiconductor manufacturer and one of only a handful of companies globally capable of producing the most advanced chips. Samsung and TSMC together dominate advanced chip fabrication.

laws.title: Korean AI Safety Framework and Generative AI Governance Act
laws.subtitle: Balancing AI innovation with safety guardrails
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted AI governance legislation establishing a risk-based regulatory framework for artificial intelligence. The law creates mandatory impact assessments for high-risk AI applications, establishes watermarking requirements for AI-generated content, creates a national AI Safety Institute, funds AI research and talent development, and establishes liability frameworks for AI-caused harms. The law is designed to be less restrictive than the EU AI Act to maintain competitiveness.
laws.penalty: AI companies that deploy high-risk systems without required safety assessments face fines up to KRW 30 million per violation. AI-generated content that falsely claims to be human-created carries up to three years imprisonment.
exceptions: Research and development AI systems in controlled laboratory environments are exempt from deployment-level requirements
Government AI systems for national security purposes operate under classified safety frameworks

quiz.q: How does South Korea's AI governance approach compare to the EU's AI Act?
options: It is stricter than the EU AI Act
It is identical to the EU AI Act
It is less restrictive to maintain competitiveness
It bans all AI development except government projects
quiz.explanation: South Korea deliberately designed its AI governance framework to be less restrictive than the EU's AI Act, wanting to maintain competitiveness with the US and China while still establishing basic safety guardrails.

laws.title: K-Pop and Korean Wave Cultural Export Promotion Act
laws.subtitle: Formalizing Hallyu as a strategic national industry
laws.fullDescription: South Korea enacted legislation formally recognizing the Korean Wave (Hallyu) — K-pop, K-dramas, Korean food, beauty, and culture — as a strategic national industry. The law creates a Korean Culture and Industry Promotion Agency with legal authority, funds K-pop talent training programs, creates visa facilitation for foreign K-culture fans, establishes intellectual property protections for Korean cultural content, and creates soft power diplomacy programs linking cultural exports to trade relationships.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized commercial exploitation of K-pop artist imagery without licensing carries up to five years imprisonment. Piracy of Korean entertainment content carries up to three years.
exceptions: Fan-created non-commercial content retains broad creative freedom protections
Academic and cultural research using Korean cultural content operates under fair use provisions

quiz.q: What term describes the global spread of South Korean popular culture including K-pop and K-dramas?
quiz.explanation: Hallyu (한류) or the 'Korean Wave' describes the global phenomenon of South Korean popular culture — K-pop, K-dramas, Korean food, beauty products, and entertainment — that has become a major soft power asset and economic driver for South Korea.

laws.title: South Korea Martial Law Crisis and Constitutional Restoration Act
laws.subtitle: Democratic Safeguard and President Accountability Law
laws.fullDescription: Enacted following President Yoon Suk-yeol's brief declaration of martial law in December 2024 that was overturned by the National Assembly within hours. The law strengthens the National Assembly's power to countermand presidential emergency declarations, establishes impeachment procedures for presidents abusing emergency powers, creates whistleblower protections for military officers refusing unlawful orders, and mandates civilian oversight of military command during political crises.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution for unconstitutional use of emergency powers; impeachment and permanent bar from public office
exceptions: Legitimate national security emergencies with parliamentary notification retained
Military may act against foreign attack without prior parliamentary approval

quiz.q: When did President Yoon Suk-yeol briefly declare martial law in South Korea?
quiz.explanation: President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law in December 2024, which the National Assembly overturned within hours.

laws.title: South Korea Chips Act and Semiconductor Cluster Expansion Law
laws.subtitle: National Semiconductor Industry Support Act
laws.fullDescription: Establishes massive government support for South Korea's semiconductor industry to maintain competitive advantage against Chinese and US rivals. The law provides 26 trillion won in subsidies and tax credits for semiconductor fab construction, creates the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster with seven new Samsung and SK Hynix fabs, establishes export controls for advanced chip technology, and funds semiconductor engineer education to address talent shortages.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution for semiconductor technology theft; fines up to 3 billion won for export control violations
exceptions: Legacy semiconductor technology (28nm+) has relaxed export controls
Academic research partnerships with security agreements
laws.sourceLabel: South Korea Ministry of Science and ICT

quiz.q: How much does South Korea's Chips Act allocate in subsidies and tax credits?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's Chips Act provides 26 trillion won in subsidies and tax credits to maintain semiconductor competitiveness.

laws.title: South Korea Yoon Impeachment and Constitutional Court Ruling Act
laws.subtitle: Presidential Removal and Democracy Restoration Law
laws.fullDescription: Governs the aftermath of President Yoon Suk-yeol's impeachment following his martial law declaration. The Constitutional Court unanimously upheld the National Assembly's impeachment in April 2025, removing Yoon from office. The law establishes the legal consequences of impeachment, creates snap presidential election frameworks, and codifies lessons learned for preventing future unconstitutional executive actions.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution for insurrection charges against Yoon; accountability for military officials involved
exceptions: Former president retains basic personal legal rights during criminal proceedings
Acting president has full executive authority during transition

quiz.q: What did South Korea's Constitutional Court decide about President Yoon's impeachment?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's Constitutional Court unanimously upheld the National Assembly's impeachment of President Yoon Suk-yeol in April 2025.

laws.title: Presidential Impeachment and Early Election
laws.subtitle: Constitutional Crisis and Democratic Resilience
laws.fullDescription: Following the impeachment of President Yoon Suk-yeol over his short-lived declaration of martial law in December 2024, South Korea held early presidential elections in June 2025. The Constitutional Court upheld the impeachment, and the Democratic Party candidate won. The episode tested constitutional order and democratic norms.
laws.penalty: Political accountability through constitutional process; no criminal penalties for voters
exceptions: Constitutional Court review process
Assembly impeachment threshold of two-thirds majority

quiz.q: What triggered South Korea's 2024 presidential impeachment?
quiz.explanation: President Yoon Suk-yeol's brief martial law declaration in December 2024 triggered the impeachment process that the Constitutional Court upheld in 2025.

laws.title: Semiconductor Alliance and CHIPS Act Cooperation
laws.subtitle: South Korea Expands US Chip Manufacturing Partnerships
laws.fullDescription: South Korea deepened semiconductor cooperation with the United States under the CHIPS and Science Act, with Samsung and SK Hynix receiving billions in grants for US manufacturing facilities. The semiconductor alliance also addressed Chinese market access restrictions and technology transfer controls.
laws.penalty: Export control violations subject to US sanctions; fine and debarment
exceptions: Technology transfer license exemptions
Allied nation provisions

quiz.q: What did Samsung and SK Hynix receive under the US CHIPS Act?
options: Billions in grants for US manufacturing facilities
quiz.explanation: Samsung and SK Hynix received billions in US government grants for building semiconductor manufacturing facilities in the United States under the CHIPS and Science Act.

laws.title: Demographic Emergency and Pro-Natalist Policies
laws.subtitle: South Korea Has World's Lowest Fertility Rate
laws.fullDescription: South Korea recorded a total fertility rate of 0.72 in 2023, the lowest of any OECD country and among the lowest in the world. The government declared a demographic emergency and expanded pro-natalist incentives including cash payments, housing priority for families, and parental leave. Young Koreans cited housing costs, education competition, and work culture as reasons not to have children.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; generous incentive programs
exceptions: Voluntary benefit programs
Immigration policy debates as supplement

quiz.q: What was South Korea's total fertility rate in 2023?
quiz.explanation: South Korea recorded a total fertility rate of 0.72 in 2023, the lowest of any OECD nation and a demographic emergency prompting major government response.

laws.title: AI Industry Promotion and Regulation Balance
laws.subtitle: South Korea Develops National AI Framework
laws.fullDescription: South Korea developed a national AI framework attempting to balance promoting its AI industry (Samsung, SK Hynix, Naver, Kakao) with safeguarding citizens from AI risks. The framework established certification for high-risk AI, supported AI chips development, and created testing facilities. Korea sought to be a major AI player beyond its chip manufacturing.
laws.penalty: Administrative fines for high-risk AI non-compliance
exceptions: Research and development exemptions
Military AI separate framework

quiz.q: Beyond chips, what AI companies is South Korea seeking to develop internationally?
options: Naver and Kakao software AI platforms
quiz.explanation: South Korea is developing Naver and Kakao as AI software platforms alongside its chip manufacturing from Samsung and SK Hynix, seeking a complete AI ecosystem.

laws.title: K-Pop and Korean Wave Cultural Export
laws.subtitle: Korea's Soft Power Transforms Global Culture
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's cultural industry continued its global dominance with BTS, BLACKPINK, and other K-pop acts generating billions in global revenue. Korean drama, gaming, beauty products, and food followed. The government formally supported the Korean Wave (Hallyu) as economic and diplomatic soft power. The cultural export economy exceeded $12 billion annually.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; intellectual property protections
exceptions: Cultural content tax credits
Artists' labor protections

quiz.q: What term describes South Korea's global cultural phenomenon?
quiz.explanation: The Korean Wave, or Hallyu, describes South Korea's global cultural phenomenon spanning K-pop, K-drama, beauty products, and food, generating over $12 billion in annual cultural exports.

laws.title: K-Content Global Dominance and Soft Power Economy
