laws.subtitle: South Korea's cultural exports reshape global entertainment
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's cultural exports — K-pop, K-dramas, Korean film, and Korean food — have become major economic drivers. The Korean Wave (Hallyu) contributes billions to the economy through music exports, tourism, cosmetics, and food. BTS and BLACKPINK generate enormous economic multipliers. Netflix invested billions in Korean content production. The Korean government treats cultural exports as strategic economic policy, funding content creation through dedicated agencies.
laws.penalty: Content creators must meet local content quotas on Korean streaming platforms
exceptions: International co-productions with majority Korean creative control qualify as Korean content
Independent productions exempt from large studio content requirements

laws.title: Yoon Suk-yeol Martial Law Declaration and Impeachment
laws.subtitle: South Korean president briefly declares martial law, then impeached
laws.fullDescription: President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law in December 2024 in an extraordinary and short-lived attempt to circumvent the opposition-controlled National Assembly. The Assembly voted to lift martial law within hours, and Yoon was subsequently impeached by the National Assembly and removed from office by the Constitutional Court. The crisis demonstrated South Korea's democratic resilience but shocked allies who depend on Korean stability. Acting presidents managed governance during the constitutional process. New elections were scheduled.
laws.penalty: Martial law declaration must be lifted if the National Assembly votes to terminate it within 24 hours
exceptions: Presidential orders during martial law have a constitutional emergency basis
Military personnel following legitimate orders during martial law period are protected from prosecution

laws.title: Battery Industry Leadership and Global Supply Chain
laws.subtitle: South Korea dominates EV battery manufacturing globally
laws.fullDescription: South Korea is home to the world's three largest EV battery manufacturers: LGES (LG Energy Solution), Samsung SDI, and SK Innovation. These companies supply Tesla, GM, Ford, Volkswagen, and most global automakers. The battery supply chain — from mining through cell production to battery management systems — is where South Korea is building strategic economic advantage. South Korean battery makers are building factories in the US under IRA incentives, Europe, and Indonesia.
laws.penalty: Companies receiving IRA battery credits must meet domestic content requirements that phase in over time
exceptions: Research and development battery production exempt from commercial domestic content requirements
Critical mineral supply chain investments receive additional IRA credits
laws.sourceLabel: Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy

quiz.q: What are the three South Korean companies that dominate global EV battery manufacturing?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's three battery giants — LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK Innovation — supply most of the world's major automakers and are building factories globally as EV adoption accelerates.

laws.title: Housing Crisis and Jeonse System Collapse
laws.subtitle: South Korea's unique lease system faces instability amid housing bubble
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's unique 'jeonse' housing system — where tenants pay a large lump sum (typically 50-70% of property value) to landlords and live rent-free — faced a crisis as housing prices fell. Landlords couldn't return jeonse deposits when apartment values dropped below the deposit amounts. Thousands of 'jeonse fraud' victims lost their life savings. The government created a compensation fund and reformed the jeonse registry system. South Korea's housing market faces affordability challenges in Seoul with some of Asia's highest prices.
laws.penalty: Landlords must maintain jeonse deposits in escrow accounts or provide guarantees under reformed law
exceptions: Short-term rental contracts under 1 year have different disclosure requirements
Public housing developments exempt from jeonse registration requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Korean Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport

quiz.q: What is the Korean 'jeonse' housing system?
options: A system where tenants pay a lump sum deposit and live rent-free
A shared housing platform like Airbnb
quiz.explanation: Jeonse is a uniquely Korean system where tenants deposit 50-70% of property value with the landlord and live rent-free — the landlord uses the deposit as an investment. It collapsed when housing prices fell below deposit values.

laws.title: Yoon Impeachment and Constitutional Crisis
laws.subtitle: South Korea's democratic resilience tested by martial law declaration
laws.fullDescription: South Korea experienced its most dramatic political crisis in decades when President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law on December 3, 2024 — the first such declaration since 1980. Yoon claimed the opposition-controlled National Assembly had paralyzed government through repeated budget rejections. The Assembly voted to overturn the martial law within hours, and Yoon rescinded it. The National Assembly then impeached Yoon with a 204-85 vote, suspending his presidential powers. The Constitutional Court unanimously upheld the impeachment in April 2025, removing Yoon from office permanently. The episode demonstrated both the fragility of South Korean democracy and its resilience — institutions successfully reversed the action within hours. South Korea faces North Korean nuclear threats, alliance management with the US, and economic pressures.
laws.penalty: Unconstitutional actions including the martial law declaration face criminal prosecution; Yoon faced charges of insurrection
exceptions: Presidential immunity applies to official acts but not to crimes against constitutional order

quiz.q: How was President Yoon's martial law declaration ended?
options: Yoon voluntarily rescinded it after 6 hours
The National Assembly voted to overturn it within hours
The military refused to enforce it
The Constitutional Court issued an emergency injunction
quiz.explanation: The National Assembly voted to overturn President Yoon's martial law declaration within hours — a remarkable demonstration of institutional resilience. He was subsequently impeached and removed by the Constitutional Court.

laws.title: K-Pop Global Influence and Cultural Soft Power
laws.subtitle: South Korea's cultural industries transforming global entertainment
laws.fullDescription: South Korea has achieved an extraordinary level of cultural soft power through its entertainment industries — K-pop, K-dramas, Korean films, Korean food, and Korean beauty (K-beauty). BTS became the world's most popular music group with unprecedented global reach. Blackpink sold out stadium tours globally. The film Parasite won the Academy Award for Best Picture in 2020 — the first non-English language film to do so. Korean dramas dominate Netflix globally across diverse markets. The Korean Wave (Hallyu) has created massive demand for Korean language learning, tourism to South Korea, and Korean cultural products. The Korean government has actively supported the cultural industry through K-Culture training centers, the Korea Creative Content Agency, and diplomatic promotion. The cultural soft power has made South Korea globally visible and influential far beyond its size.
laws.penalty: Copyright laws protect Korean cultural content globally; idol management contracts have been scrutinized for exploitative terms
exceptions: Some cultural content exempt from Korean censorship requirements for international platforms

quiz.q: What was historically significant about the film Parasite at the 2020 Academy Awards?
options: It was the first South Korean film nominated for Best Picture
It was the first non-English language film to win Best Picture
It was the most commercially successful foreign language film in US history
It was the first film from Asia to win the Palme d'Or and Best Picture in the same year
quiz.explanation: Parasite (directed by Bong Joon-ho) won the Academy Award for Best Picture at the 2020 Oscars — the first non-English language film ever to win the top prize in the 92-year history of the Academy Awards.

laws.title: Yoon Martial Law Crisis
laws.subtitle: President's brief martial law declaration triggers impeachment
laws.fullDescription: President Yoon Suk-yeol shocked South Korea and the world by declaring martial law in December 2024, claiming the opposition-controlled National Assembly was conducting anti-state activities. The Assembly voted to lift martial law within hours, and Yoon reversed course. The Constitutional Court subsequently upheld his impeachment in April 2025, removing him from office. The crisis was the most serious constitutional emergency in South Korea since the 1980s and led to early presidential elections.
laws.penalty: Martial law lifted by National Assembly vote within hours; Yoon's executive orders during martial law period nullified
exceptions: Military personnel who followed orders during brief martial law period largely not prosecuted
Constitutional court process provided orderly resolution
laws.sourceLabel: Office of the President of Korea

quiz.q: How quickly did South Korea's National Assembly vote to lift President Yoon's martial law declaration?
quiz.explanation: The National Assembly voted to lift martial law within hours of Yoon's declaration, demonstrating the strength of South Korea's democratic institutions against executive overreach.

laws.title: Semiconductor National Strategy and CHIPS Race
laws.subtitle: Korea protects chip industry from geopolitical competition
laws.fullDescription: South Korea is the world's largest memory chip producer through Samsung and SK Hynix, with a dominant position in DRAM and NAND flash. The US CHIPS Act and Chinese investment restrictions created pressure on Korean companies to choose sides. The US pushed Korean chipmakers not to expand Chinese operations significantly. Korea negotiated its own chip industry support packages. The semiconductor industry is so central to Korean economic security that it has become a foreign policy and national security issue.
laws.penalty: Korean companies must comply with US export controls to maintain access to US equipment; violations risk significant business disruption
exceptions: Existing Chinese fab operations allowed to continue under verified end-user controls
R&D collaboration with allies encouraged under chip alliance frameworks
laws.sourceLabel: Korean Ministry of Science and ICT

quiz.q: What are the two dominant Korean companies in global memory chip production?
quiz.explanation: Samsung and SK Hynix are the two dominant Korean companies in global memory chip production, giving South Korea a strategic position in the global semiconductor supply chain that has become a major national security concern.

laws.title: K-Gaming and Esports Global Dominance
laws.subtitle: South Korea's gaming culture creates global esports industry
laws.fullDescription: South Korea pioneered competitive gaming as a spectator sport, with Starcraft matches broadcast on dedicated TV channels in the early 2000s. Korean players dominate global esports competitions in League of Legends, StarCraft, Overwatch and many other titles. Korean gaming companies including Nexon, NCSoft and Krafton (PUBG) are global publishers. The Korean government has invested in esports infrastructure and the country's broadband infrastructure enabled gaming culture that preceded the global broadband era. Gaming addiction treatment is also a focus given heavy youth gaming.
laws.penalty: Game addiction designation allows courts to order treatment; youth access to games restricted after midnight
exceptions: Professional esports players have different status from recreational gamers
Adult gaming platforms exempt from youth-focused midnight shutdown

quiz.q: Which South Korean game became the world's most-watched battle royale and was developed by Krafton?
quiz.explanation: PUBG (PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds), developed by Krafton in South Korea, pioneered the battle royale genre and became one of the world's most-played games, representing South Korea's significant contribution to global gaming culture.

laws.title: Hyundai Kia EV Global Expansion
laws.subtitle: South Korea's automakers challenge Tesla with Ioniq and EV6
laws.fullDescription: Hyundai-Kia has emerged as one of the most competitive electric vehicle manufacturers globally, with the Ioniq 5, Ioniq 6 and Kia EV6 winning major industry awards and capturing significant market share. South Korea is building a domestic EV battery supply chain and has attracted US investment under the Inflation Reduction Act's battery manufacturing incentives. Hyundai is building a major EV and battery factory in Georgia. South Korea's automotive sector has successfully navigated the EV transition better than many legacy automakers.
laws.penalty: EV manufacturers must comply with US CAFE standards and IRA domestic content requirements for subsidies
exceptions: Free trade agreement provisions affect IRA eligibility calculations
Commercial vehicles have different standards than passenger cars

quiz.q: What Hyundai vehicle was among the first to challenge Tesla significantly in the premium EV market?
quiz.explanation: The Hyundai Ioniq 5 was among the first vehicles to seriously challenge Tesla's premium EV dominance, winning multiple car of the year awards and helping establish Hyundai-Kia as one of the world's most competitive EV manufacturers.

laws.title: Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth Act
laws.subtitle: K-Green New Deal
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's 2021 Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth Act, passed following youth climate protests, set a 40% emissions reduction by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2050. South Korea is the world's 9th largest greenhouse gas emitter and was the last major OECD economy still building coal plants. The 'K-Green New Deal' includes green infrastructure, electric vehicles, and offshore wind. South Korea also passed legislation requiring ESG disclosure and climate risk reporting for major corporations. Seoul has been recognized for its urban green space restoration, including the Cheonggyecheon Stream project.
laws.penalty: Fines for major emitters failing sector targets; ETS compliance costs under Korea's emissions trading system
exceptions: POSCO and steel sector transition period
Defense and strategic industries under modified requirements

laws.title: Korean National Health Insurance
laws.subtitle: Fast Universal Coverage Achievement
laws.fullDescription: South Korea achieved universal health coverage in just 12 years (1977-1989) — one of the fastest expansions in history. The National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) covers all residents under a single public insurer, with premium contributions based on income. South Korea has extraordinarily high rates of cancer screening, with national programs detecting cancers early. Korea's healthcare technology is world-leading — Samsung Medical Center, Asan Medical Center, and Severance Hospital rank among Asia's best. Korea's digital health records and e-healthcare systems are internationally recognized models.
laws.penalty: NHIS contributions mandatory; employers liable for employee enrollment; non-payment pursued aggressively
exceptions: Medical aid (Medicaid equivalent) for low-income residents covered by state
Foreign residents must enroll after 6 months

laws.title: Korean 52-Hour Workweek and Gig Economy
laws.subtitle: From 68 Hours to Work-Life Balance
laws.fullDescription: South Korea reduced its maximum working week from 68 hours to 52 hours (40 regular + 12 overtime), phased in between 2018-2021. Korea had the second-longest working hours in the OECD — the culture of 'ppalli ppalli' (hurry hurry) and mandatory after-work drinking sessions (hoesik) was embedded in corporate culture. The 52-hour limit aimed to create jobs by spreading work. Korea also faces debates over gig worker classification — delivery app workers and platform workers have organized. Korea's minimum wage has risen significantly: KRW 9,860/hour (2024). Yoon government sought to relax 52-hour rules.
laws.penalty: Exceeding 52-hour limit: Labor Minister can suspend business; fines up to 20 million won per violation
exceptions: 5-30 person companies had delayed implementation
Some specialized industries may have weekly variance averaging

laws.title: Hagwon Regulation Law
laws.subtitle: South Korea's private tutoring cram school controls
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Act on the Establishment and Operation of Private Teaching Institutes regulates over 100,000 hagwons (private cram schools) attended by 70%+ of Korean students. The law caps operating hours (banned after 10 PM in most areas), requires fee disclosures, mandates safety standards, and attempts to curb the 'education fever' driving household debt. Despite regulations, the private tutoring market exceeds ₩26 trillion annually, fueling inequality.
laws.penalty: Hagwons operating past curfew fined up to 5 million KRW; repeat violations result in closure orders
exceptions: Adult education hagwons exempt from 10 PM curfew
Online tutoring platforms face different regulations
laws.sourceLabel: Act on Establishment and Operation of Private Teaching Institutes

quiz.q: What time do South Korean regulations typically require hagwons (cram schools) to close?
quiz.explanation: Most Korean local governments enforce a 10 PM closing time for hagwons under the Private Teaching Institutes Act, though enforcement varies and the rule is frequently violated.

laws.title: Immigration Act and E-9 Agricultural Visa
laws.subtitle: South Korea's managed labor migration system
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Immigration Act manages a sophisticated system of work visas for its labor-short economy. The E-9 visa (Employment Permit System) brings workers from 16 countries (including Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, Cambodia) for agricultural, manufacturing, and fishing sectors. The F-4 ethnic Korean (gyopo) visa allows overseas Koreans easier residency. South Korea has resisted large-scale immigration despite severe demographic decline (world's lowest birth rate). Approximately 2 million foreign workers are in South Korea, facing documented issues of wage theft and abuse especially in agriculture.
laws.penalty: Visa overstayers (approximately 400,000 in South Korea) may be detained and deported; employers abusing foreign workers face labor law penalties; human trafficking carries 1-10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Ethnic Koreans (Korean-Chinese H-2 visa) have easier work rights
F-5 permanent residency available after 5 years with income and integration requirements
laws.sourceLabel: South Korea Immigration Act and Employment Permit System

quiz.q: South Korea's E-9 visa (Employment Permit System) recruits workers from how many designated countries?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's EPS (Employment Permit System) recruits workers from 16 designated countries including Vietnam, Philippines, Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, Mongolia, and others for sectors like manufacturing, agriculture, fisheries, and construction.

laws.title: Narcotics Control Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's strict drug laws and global jurisdiction
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Narcotics Control Act imposes extremely strict penalties and is unique in claiming extraterritorial jurisdiction — Korean citizens can be prosecuted in South Korea for drug offenses committed abroad, including in countries where the activity is legal (such as using cannabis in Colorado, USA, or Amsterdam). This leads to celebrity prosecutions — famous actors and athletes have received criminal charges for admitting cannabis use abroad. Drug trafficking carries up to life imprisonment. South Korea has very low drug use rates. The government has resisted any drug liberalization.
laws.penalty: Cannabis possession: up to 5 years; marijuana use abroad by Korean citizen: prosecutable in Korea; trafficking: up to life imprisonment; heroin/cocaine trafficking (organized): life or death penalty possible for large quantities
exceptions: Medical use of specific narcotics under strict prescription
Industrial hemp cultivation in limited licensed areas
No decriminalization for any recreational use

quiz.q: South Korea can prosecute its citizens for drug offenses committed in other countries where the drugs are legal. What is this legal principle called?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's Narcotics Control Act has extraterritorial jurisdiction — meaning Korean citizens can be prosecuted in Korea for drug use that occurred abroad, even in jurisdictions where that drug use was completely legal (like cannabis in US states or Netherlands).

laws.title: No Legal Recognition — Military Sodomy Law Under Challenge
laws.subtitle: South Korea lacks LGBTQ+ protections and criminalizes same-sex conduct in military
laws.fullDescription: South Korea does not recognize same-sex relationships and has no national anti-discrimination law protecting sexual orientation, despite years of legislative attempts. Article 92-6 of the Military Criminal Act criminalizes consensual same-sex conduct among service members, with penalties up to 2 years imprisonment. The Constitutional Court has twice upheld this provision (2011, 2023) despite LGBTQ+ advocacy. Seoul Pride has been held since 2000 but faces counter-protests. Public opinion is shifting, particularly among younger Koreans. Several politicians have run on LGBTQ+-rights platforms.
laws.penalty: Military personnel convicted under Article 92-6 face up to 2 years imprisonment; no civil hate crime protections
exceptions: Civilian same-sex conduct is not criminalized

quiz.q: What does South Korea's Military Criminal Act Article 92-6 criminalize?
options: Consensual same-sex conduct among service members
quiz.explanation: Article 92-6 of South Korea's Military Criminal Act criminalizes consensual same-sex conduct among service members with up to 2 years imprisonment, a provision upheld by the Constitutional Court in both 2011 and 2023.

laws.title: Press Freedom Improvements With Remaining Challenges
laws.subtitle: South Korea has a free press tradition but defamation laws and political pressures persist
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's constitution (Article 21) guarantees freedom of speech and press. South Korea has a vibrant media landscape including JoongAng, Chosun Ilbo, Hankyoreh, KBS, and MBC. Press freedom has improved significantly since democratization in 1987. However, criminal defamation law allows prosecution even when the published information is true, if it harms reputation — a significant press freedom concern. During conservative administrations, public broadcasters faced political pressure. The Yonhap news agency is the dominant wire service. Online defamation prosecutions have increased with social media.
laws.penalty: Criminal defamation law applies even to true statements if damaging to reputation; civil defamation suits common
exceptions: Truth is a defense if public interest is served, but courts have applied this inconsistently

quiz.q: What unusual aspect of South Korea's criminal defamation law creates press freedom concerns?
options: It applies to foreign journalists only
It can prosecute for true statements if they harm reputation
quiz.explanation: South Korea's criminal defamation law can apply even when the published statement is true — if it damages someone's reputation and is not deemed in the public interest, the journalist can face criminal prosecution, creating a significant chilling effect on investigative journalism.

laws.title: Personal Information Protection Act and Platform Regulation
laws.subtitle: South Korea has comprehensive data protection and has fined major tech platforms
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) is one of Asia's strongest data protection laws, amended significantly in 2023. The Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) enforces PIPA. South Korea fined Google (82 billion KRW, ~$63M) and Meta (30.8 billion KRW, ~$23M) in 2022 for illegally collecting user information without consent. South Korea's Telecommunications Business Act has provisions on platform content moderation. South Korea has been active in AI governance through the Framework Act on Artificial Intelligence (2025). Online defamation using real identity is easier to prosecute under real-name registration systems.
laws.penalty: PIPA: fines up to 3% of revenue for violations; PIPC enforcement authority; major fines against Google and Meta
exceptions: Research and journalism exemptions apply

quiz.q: How much did South Korea fine Google in 2022 for illegally collecting user information?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's PIPC fined Google approximately $63 million (82 billion KRW) in 2022 for illegally collecting user information without proper consent — one of Asia's largest data protection fines, alongside a $23 million fine against Meta for similar violations.

laws.title: FSC Real-Name Crypto Rule & Bank-Crypto Partnership
laws.subtitle: South Korea requires real-name bank accounts linked to all crypto trading
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Financial Services Commission (FSC) implemented the 'real-name verification system' for cryptocurrency: all crypto exchange users must link a real-name verified bank account from a partnered bank to their exchange account. This effectively gives major banks veto power over which exchanges can operate at scale (only a few major banks partner with crypto exchanges). The Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) requires all virtual asset service providers (VASPs) to register. South Korea's Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (ARUSFTI) governs crypto AML. The FSC also tightened household debt limits following rapid credit growth.
laws.penalty: Unregistered VASP operation: fines up to KRW 30 million or 5 years imprisonment; real-name system violations by exchanges: license revocation; individual AML violations: fines and criminal charges
exceptions: Professional investors have modified account requirements
Institutional trading accounts may bypass retail real-name requirements
Exempt tokens used within specific platforms may have modified rules

quiz.q: What unique requirement does South Korea impose on cryptocurrency traders not common in most countries?
options: Crypto profits must be held for 1 year before withdrawal
All traders must link a real-name bank account from a partnered bank to their exchange
Crypto can only be traded through licensed brokers, not exchanges
All crypto must be converted to won weekly
quiz.explanation: South Korea requires all crypto exchange users to link a real-name verified bank account from a bank that has officially partnered with the exchange — effectively giving banks control over which exchanges can serve retail customers.

laws.title: MFDS Food Safety & Kimchi Fermentation Standards
laws.subtitle: South Korea protects kimchi as cultural heritage with strict quality and origin standards
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) regulates food safety comprehensively. Kimchi — South Korea's most iconic food — is subject to detailed MFDS standards covering fermentation time, ingredients, labeling, and production conditions. South Korea fought a trade dispute with China over kimchi authenticity (Chinese-made kimchi: 'pao cai' vs. Korean kimchi: 'kimchi'), winning an ISO standard (ISO 11576) recognizing Korean kimchi's distinct cultural and production identity. South Korea requires front-of-pack nutrition labeling on all processed food. The country has strict food additive standards and bans several dyes and preservatives permitted in other countries. Korean school meals follow strict nutrition guidelines with fresh food preparation requirements.
laws.penalty: MFDS food violations: fines up to KRW 30 million; false kimchi origin labeling (selling Chinese kimchi as Korean): significant fines and recall; food safety violations causing illness: criminal prosecution
exceptions: Traditional home kimchi production for personal consumption is unregulated
Restaurant kimchi made on-premises has modified labeling requirements
Agricultural cooperatives directly selling own-produced kimchi have simplified MFDS registration

quiz.q: What international standards dispute did South Korea win regarding kimchi identity?
options: WTO ruling that China must pay tariffs on kimchi exports to Korea
ISO standard (ISO 11576) recognizing Korean kimchi as distinct from Chinese pao cai
UN UNESCO intangible cultural heritage designation blocking Chinese imitation
CODEX Alimentarius standard defining kimchi's Korean origin
quiz.explanation: South Korea secured ISO 11576:2021 — an international standard specifically for Korean kimchi — following controversy over China claiming its 'pao cai' (pickled vegetables) was equivalent to kimchi. The ISO standard validated kimchi's distinct Korean cultural and culinary identity, distinguishing it from Chinese pickled vegetable products.

laws.title: South Korea Animal Protection Act — Dog Meat Ban 2024
laws.subtitle: South Korea banned the dog meat industry in 2024
laws.fullDescription: South Korea made global headlines in January 2024 when the National Assembly passed a law banning the breeding, slaughtering, and selling of dogs for human consumption — effective 2027 (with a 3-year phase-out). The Animal Protection Act (amended through 2024) criminalizes animal cruelty, mandates registration and microchipping of dogs and cats, and restricts pet store sales. South Korea has faced international criticism for its dog meat industry (gaegogi). The country's K-pet culture has grown enormously — over 15 million pets — creating cultural shift away from dog meat. South Korea also bans animal fighting, restricts exotic pets, and has active enforcement by animal protection organizations partnering with police.
laws.penalty: Animal cruelty: up to 3 years imprisonment or 30 million KRW fine; dog meat trade violations (post-2027): up to 3 years; abandonment: up to 300,000 KRW fine
exceptions: Livestock farming under veterinary standards
Licensed hunting
Scientific research with IACUC approval
Dog meat trade permitted until 2027 phase-out

quiz.q: What historic decision did South Korea's National Assembly make in January 2024?
options: Banning the dog meat industry (breeding, slaughtering, selling) effective 2027
Requiring all pets to be imported
Creating a national pet health insurance scheme
quiz.explanation: In January 2024, South Korea's National Assembly passed a law banning the entire dog meat industry — breeding, slaughtering, distributing, and selling dogs for human consumption — with a 3-year phase-out period ending the long-criticized practice in the world's 12th largest economy.

laws.title: South Korea Family Law — Household Registry Reform and Marriage Equality Debate
laws.subtitle: Korea abolished patriarchal family register system in 2005
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's family law is governed by the Civil Act (Minbeop). South Korea abolished its controversial 'hoju' (patriarchal household registry) system in 2005, replacing it with individual-based registration — a significant feminist achievement. Divorce rates are high and rising. Divorce by agreement (hyeopsso離婚) can be processed administratively; contested divorces require court proceedings. Korea's Supreme Court and Constitutional Court have issued important family law rulings — including on division of pension rights between divorcing spouses (2014). South Korea's Constitutional Court declared the prohibition on same-sex marriage constitutional in 2024, though lower courts have issued rulings in favor of same-sex recognition for health insurance. Korean family courts use 'chinyŏk' (best interests) standard for children.
laws.penalty: Civil enforcement through gajŏng bŏpwŏn (family courts); alimony and child support enforced; wage garnishment; criminal domestic violence charges
exceptions: Prenuptial agreements (hon-jeon gyeyak)
Pre-marital property retained
Separate property designation available

quiz.q: What patriarchal family registry system did South Korea abolish in 2005?
options: The hoju (patriarchal household head registry) system — which listed all family members under the male head's name
quiz.explanation: South Korea abolished its 'hoju' (家主) system in 2005 — a traditional patriarchal registry that organized all family members under the male household head's name. The system was criticized as reinforcing gender discrimination and was replaced with individual-based civil registration, a landmark feminist legal reform.

laws.title: South Korea Jeonse System & Lease Act
laws.subtitle: Unique jeonse deposit-lease system and tenant rights
laws.fullDescription: South Korea has a unique 'jeonse' housing rental system where tenants pay a large lump-sum deposit (typically 50-80% of property value) instead of monthly rent, with the landlord using the capital. The Housing Lease Protection Act (1981) protects jeonse tenants, giving them priority over creditors in case of foreclosure. The 2020 amendments under Moon Jae-in extended jeonse contracts to a minimum 4-year term and limited rent (or jeonse price) increases to 5% every two years — but this caused market disruptions and the jeonse shortage known as 'jeonse crisis.' The Real Estate Transaction Reporting Act requires all transactions to be reported.
laws.penalty: Jeonse fraud (landlord can't return deposit): criminal prosecution for fraud; illegal rent increase above 5% cap: void
exceptions: Jeonse crisis: deposit fraud cases increased dramatically 2022-2023
Priority registration protects jeonse tenant deposits against creditors
laws.sourceLabel: South Korea Jeonse Housing Lease System

quiz.q: What is the unique South Korean housing arrangement where tenants pay a large lump-sum deposit instead of monthly rent?
quiz.explanation: Jeonse is South Korea's unique deposit-lease system where tenants pay a large lump sum (typically 50-80% of property value) to live rent-free, with the landlord using the capital and returning the full deposit at lease end.

laws.title: South Korea Consumer Protection Act & KFTC
laws.subtitle: E-commerce consumer rights and financial consumer protection
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Framework Act on Consumers (2006) and Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce (2002, amended 2023) provide comprehensive protections. The Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) is the primary enforcement body. Online consumers have a 7-day withdrawal right without reason. The 2023 amendments to e-commerce consumer law addressed dark patterns and live-commerce shopping fraud. The Financial Consumer Protection Act (2021) specifically protects financial product buyers with a 15-day cooling-off period. South Korea's advanced mobile commerce market has driven innovative consumer protection rules for app stores, subscriptions, and digital content. The Consumer Affairs Agency Korea handles class complaints.
laws.penalty: KFTC fine: up to 3% of relevant turnover; e-commerce dark patterns: administrative fine and corrective orders
exceptions: 7-day e-commerce withdrawal right without reason required
Financial Consumer Protection Act 2021: 15-day cooling-off for financial products
laws.source: Framework Act on Consumers 2006; E-Commerce Act 2002 (amended 2023)

quiz.q: What specific problem did South Korea's 2023 e-commerce law amendments address in the online shopping sector?
options: Dark patterns and live-commerce shopping fraud
quiz.explanation: South Korea's 2023 amendments to the E-Commerce Consumer Protection Act specifically targeted dark patterns (manipulative design tricks) and fraud in live-commerce streaming shopping — where hosts sell products in real-time video streams, a format that has seen widespread fraud and misleading practices.

laws.title: 대한민국 헌법 — Constitution of South Korea
laws.subtitle: South Korea's democratic constitution and Constitutional Court
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Constitution (1987) was born from the June Democratic Uprising against military dictator Chun Doo-hwan. It established a presidential republic with a directly elected president limited to a single 5-year term — a safeguard against the extended rule seen under previous presidents. The Constitutional Court (헌법재판소) reviews the constitutionality of laws, adjudicates impeachment cases, and has dissolved political parties. Notably, it upheld the impeachment of President Park Geun-hye in 2017 following the Choi Soon-sil corruption scandal. The National Assembly (300 seats) exercises strong legislative oversight.
laws.penalty: Constitutional violations reviewed by Constitutional Court. Presidential impeachment requires National Assembly 2/3 vote plus Constitutional Court confirmation.
exceptions: Emergency powers under Article 77 allow presidential martial law — used controversially in December 2024
Constitutional amendments require 2/3 National Assembly vote plus national referendum
EU and international treaty obligations interpreted consistently with Constitution

quiz.q: What constitutional safeguard prevents another extended presidential regime in South Korea?
options: Presidents are limited to a single 5-year term with no re-election allowed
Presidents serve 4-year terms with maximum of 2 terms
The president is purely ceremonial with no real power
quiz.explanation: After decades of authoritarian rule, South Korea's 1987 Constitution limits the president to a single 5-year term — making re-election constitutionally impossible. This prevents the accumulation of power that enabled previous military-backed regimes. The Constitutional Court also showed its independence by removing President Park Geun-hye in 2017.

laws.title: 국가보안법 — National Security Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's controversial Cold War-era anti-communist law
laws.fullDescription: The National Security Act (NSA, 1948) criminalizes 'anti-state' activities including praising or benefiting North Korea. Critics argue it is used to suppress legitimate political dissent, labor movements, and journalism. The UN Human Rights Committee has repeatedly called for its repeal or significant reform. Activities such as possessing pro-DPRK literature, meeting North Koreans without authorization, or expressing sympathy with the North Korean government can lead to prosecution. South Korea's spy agency (NIS — National Intelligence Service) enforces this law. The NSA has resulted in convictions of academics, journalists, and political activists.
laws.penalty: Anti-state activities: up to 7 years imprisonment. Espionage benefiting enemy: up to life imprisonment. Incitement: up to 5 years.
exceptions: Academic research on North Korea is permitted with appropriate authorization
Humanitarian visits to North Korea require government approval
Journalists covering North Korea for news purposes have some protection

quiz.q: What does South Korea's National Security Act primarily criminalize?
options: Activities deemed to benefit North Korea including possession of pro-DPRK materials — a Cold War relic criticized internationally
quiz.explanation: The National Security Act criminalizes activities that 'benefit' the anti-state organization (North Korea), including possessing sympathetic materials, unauthorized contact with North Koreans, and spreading 'false facts' beneficial to the enemy. The UN Human Rights Committee has called it a threat to free expression and recommended its abolition.

laws.title: 개인정보 보호법 — Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA)
laws.subtitle: South Korea's comprehensive data protection law — among Asia's strictest
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's PIPA (2011, significantly amended 2023) is considered one of Asia's most comprehensive data protection frameworks, often compared to GDPR. The Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) enforces the law. PIPA requires: specific consent for collection, purpose limitation, data minimization, and breach notification within 72 hours for major breaches. The 2023 amendments introduced mandatory data protection officers for high-risk processors, expanded data subject rights, and increased fines. South Korea's tech giants (Samsung, Kakao, Naver) face significant compliance obligations. South Korea was recognized by the EU as having adequate data protection for cross-border transfers.
laws.penalty: Violations: fines up to 3% of related revenue. Criminal penalties: up to 5 years imprisonment or fines up to 50 million KRW. PIPC can order processing suspension.
exceptions: Public institutions processing for official purposes have modified requirements
Research and statistical use with pseudonymization has derogations
National security processing is exempt

quiz.q: What international recognition did South Korea receive regarding its data protection framework?
options: South Korea was sanctioned for insufficient data protection
South Korea was recognized by the EU as having adequate data protection for cross-border transfers
South Korea joined GDPR as a non-EU member
South Korea was first in Asia to adopt GDPR verbatim
quiz.explanation: The EU recognized South Korea as providing an adequate level of personal data protection in 2021, meaning personal data can flow freely between the EU and South Korea without additional safeguards. This was the first adequacy decision for an Asian country and reflects South Korea's PIPA being considered broadly equivalent to GDPR standards.

laws.title: 근로기준법 — Labor Standards Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's labor law and 52-hour workweek reform
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Labor Standards Act governs employment conditions. South Korea famously had among the world's longest working hours — averaging 2,000+ hours per year. The 52-hour maximum workweek was implemented in 2018 (for large firms) and phased in for smaller companies. Despite this reform, 'popchari' (compulsory social overtime) and presenteeism culture mean actual hours often exceed legal limits. South Korea's minimum wage is set annually by the Minimum Wage Commission. Workers' rights include: 15 days annual leave (after 1 year), severance pay (equivalent to 1 month per year worked), and mandatory social insurance. Chaebols' dominance creates power imbalances in employment.
laws.penalty: Working hours violations: fines up to 20 million KRW. Failure to pay minimum wage: imprisonment up to 3 years. Non-payment of severance: criminal liability.
exceptions: Businesses under 5 employees have lighter requirements
Managerial employees are exempt from working hour limits
Transportation and healthcare have sector-specific rules
laws.sourceLabel: 고용노동부 — Ministry of Employment and Labor

quiz.q: What maximum workweek did South Korea introduce in 2018 to address overwork culture?
quiz.explanation: South Korea introduced a 52-hour maximum workweek in 2018 — including a maximum 40 regular hours plus 12 hours overtime — replacing the previous de facto standard of 68 hours. The reform targeted South Korea's extreme work culture but implementation has been uneven, with workplace culture still driving excessive hours in many sectors, particularly tech and finance.

laws.title: 탄소중립기본법 — Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's legally binding 2050 carbon neutrality commitment
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Carbon Neutrality Act (2021) — the world's 14th country to pass such legislation — sets legally binding carbon neutrality by 2050 and a 40% reduction by 2030 (vs 2018 levels). South Korea is one of the world's largest greenhouse gas emitters per capita, heavily dependent on coal. The act establishes the Presidential Committee on Carbon Neutrality. South Korea accelerated offshore wind development and aims to phase out coal by 2050. Samsung, Hyundai, and other conglomerates face significant decarbonization requirements. Korea's Green New Deal includes hydrogen economy development — Hyundai is a global leader in hydrogen fuel cell vehicles.
laws.penalty: Companies in ETS (Emissions Trading System) face penalties for non-compliance. Industrial facilities violating environmental standards: significant fines and permit suspension.
exceptions: Critical industrial facilities have transition periods
Small and medium enterprises have lighter compliance timelines
Emergency energy security situations allow temporary carbon limit adjustments

quiz.q: What reduction target did South Korea commit to under its Carbon Neutrality Act?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's Carbon Neutrality Act commits to reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 40% by 2030 compared to 2018 levels, and reaching carbon neutrality by 2050. South Korea updated its NDC (Nationally Determined Contribution) under the Paris Agreement to this 40% target, up from an earlier 26.3% target.

laws.title: 국민건강보험법 — National Health Insurance Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's single-payer universal health insurance system
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's National Health Insurance (NHI) system, established 1977 and made universal in 1989, provides comprehensive coverage to all citizens and registered foreign residents. The NHI Service (NHIS) operates as a single public insurer. Premiums are income-based (approximately 7.09% of income, shared between employer and employee for workers). Coverage includes: outpatient care, hospitalization, prescription drugs, mental health, and dental. South Korea has among Asia's best healthcare outcomes with life expectancy around 84 years. COVID-19 testing and treatment were covered by NHI. Medical tourism is significant — foreigners come for cosmetic surgery, cancer treatment, and joint replacements.
laws.penalty: Non-enrolled residents: back-premiums plus penalties. Fraudulent claims: repayment plus criminal prosecution. Healthcare providers billing fraud: license suspension.
exceptions: Long-term foreign residents (over 6 months) are compulsorily enrolled
Overseas Koreans have simplified enrollment
Emergency care provided regardless of insurance status

quiz.q: When did South Korea achieve universal health insurance coverage?
quiz.explanation: South Korea achieved universal health insurance coverage in 1989, extending NHI to the self-employed and rural populations after starting with large enterprise workers in 1977. The process took 12 years from partial to universal coverage. South Korea's NHI is now a reference model for developing countries seeking to implement universal health coverage.

laws.title: 공정거래법 — Fair Trade Act and Chaebol Regulation
laws.subtitle: South Korea's competition law targeting chaebol conglomerate power
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's economy is dominated by chaebols — family-controlled industrial conglomerates (Samsung, Hyundai, SK, LG, Lotte). The Fair Trade Act and special chaebol regulations aim to limit their market power, cross-shareholding, and family control. The Fair Trade Commission (FTC) designates 'large business groups' with special obligations including: restricting circular shareholding, requiring board transparency, and limiting intra-group transactions. Chaebol families have repeatedly faced criminal charges for embezzlement, bribery, and tax evasion — often receiving pardons (presidential pardons of chaebol heirs are a recurring controversy). Samsung Chairman Lee Jae-yong was convicted twice for bribery.
laws.penalty: Anti-competitive practices: fines up to 10% of related turnover. Circular shareholding violations: divestiture orders. Chaebol executives: criminal prosecution for fraud, embezzlement.
exceptions: Intra-group transactions at arm's length with proper disclosure are permitted
Financial subsidiaries have separate regulatory treatment
Smaller business groups are exempt from large business group obligations

quiz.q: What is a 'chaebol' and why is it regulated specially in South Korea?
options: A family-controlled industrial conglomerate (Samsung, Hyundai, LG etc.) with special regulations due to their dominance over the economy
quiz.explanation: Chaebols are South Korea's family-controlled conglomerates that dominate the economy. Samsung alone accounts for about 20% of South Korea's exports. Their interlocking ownership, family control, and political connections have led to special regulations under Korea's Fair Trade Act targeting circular shareholding, intra-group transactions, and requiring greater transparency of the controlling family's power.

laws.title: 교육기본법 / 학원법 — Education Act and Private Tutoring Regulation
laws.subtitle: South Korea's intense education system and hagwon private academy regulation
laws.fullDescription: South Korea has one of the world's most intense education systems — centered on the suneung (CSAT — university entrance exam) that determines students' futures. The hagwon (private tutoring academy) industry is massive — families spend 20%+ of income on private education. The government has repeatedly tried to regulate hagwons: curfews limiting operations to 10 PM, curriculum restrictions, and price controls on fees. Despite regulations, the industry exceeds 20 trillion KRW annually. University entrance competition drives extreme studying — South Korea has documented problems with student mental health and suicide linked to academic pressure. The PISA scores consistently rank South Korea among the world's top performers.
laws.penalty: Hagwon operating beyond 10 PM: business closure orders, fines. Operating without registration: significant fines. Student safety violations: license revocation.
exceptions: Online tutoring platforms have different operating rules
Adult education programs are exempt from curfews
Special education for disabled students has modified rules

quiz.q: What is the significance of the 'suneung' in South Korean society?
options: The university entrance exam that largely determines educational and career paths — one of the most high-stakes tests in the world
A national fitness assessment for military service
A licensing exam for professional jobs
quiz.explanation: The Suneung (수능 — College Scholastic Ability Test) is South Korea's annual university entrance exam held in November. On exam day, planes avoid flying over testing centers, stock markets open late, and police escort late students. A single point difference can determine which university a student attends, making it one of the world's highest-stakes examinations with documented mental health impacts.

laws.title: 금융소비자보호법 — Financial Consumer Protection Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's law protecting investors after derivatives mis-selling scandals
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's Financial Consumer Protection Act (2021) was enacted following major derivatives mis-selling scandals — particularly DLF (Derivatives-Linked Fund) products sold to retail investors by major banks in 2019, causing losses of hundreds of billions of KRW for elderly investors who did not understand the products. The act requires: six-stage suitability assessment before selling complex products, mandatory cooling-off periods (7-14 days), stronger post-sale obligations, and severe penalties for unsuitable sales. The FSC (Financial Services Commission) and FSS (Financial Supervisory Service) jointly enforce financial consumer protections. Korea's financial regulators also supervise one of the world's most active retail stock trading markets.
laws.penalty: Unsuitable sales: full compensation to investor plus fines. KRW 50 billion cap per incident for serious violations. Executive-level criminal liability for systematic violations.
exceptions: Professional investors (institutional) have lighter protections
Products below certain complexity thresholds have simplified requirements
OTC derivatives between institutional parties follow ISDA framework

quiz.q: What specific scandal prompted South Korea to pass its Financial Consumer Protection Act in 2021?
options: DLF (Derivatives-Linked Fund) mis-selling by major banks to retail investors in 2019, causing major losses for elderly customers
quiz.explanation: The 2019 DLF scandal revealed that major Korean banks (Woori, Hana) sold complex interest-rate-linked derivatives to elderly retail investors without proper explanation of risks. When global interest rates fell, investors — many of them retirees — lost up to 100% of their investment. The scandal triggered the 2021 Financial Consumer Protection Act requiring extensive suitability assessments.

laws.title: 부패방지 및 청렴위원회법 / 김영란법 — Anti-Corruption Laws
laws.subtitle: South Korea's Kim Young-ran Act restricting gifts to public officials
laws.fullDescription: The Kim Young-ran Act (2016) — named after the former Chief Justice who proposed it — prohibits giving or receiving gifts, meals, or entertainment above strict thresholds to public officials, journalists, and teachers: meals over 30,000 KRW (~$23), gifts over 50,000 KRW, and event tickets over 100,000 KRW. The law was controversial — restaurant and gift industries lobbied against it. It applies to spouses of covered persons as well. The Act has significantly changed corporate entertainment culture in South Korea. The Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission (ACRC) oversees compliance. South Korea's ranking on Transparency International's CPI has improved since the law's passage.
laws.penalty: Offering or receiving prohibited gifts: fines up to 30 million KRW. Criminal prosecution possible. Fines based on 2-5x the value of the benefit received.
exceptions: Gifts under legal thresholds within normal social customs are permitted
Agricultural/fishery products from government programs have higher limits
Donations to nonprofits follow separate rules

quiz.q: What maximum meal value can be given to a public official, journalist, or teacher under the Kim Young-ran Act?
quiz.explanation: The Kim Young-ran Act (청탁금지법) sets a maximum meal value of 30,000 KRW (~$23) for public officials, journalists, and private school teachers. Gifts are capped at 50,000 KRW and congratulatory/condolence money at 100,000 KRW. Exceeding these amounts — even in a social setting — is illegal for both the giver and receiver.

laws.title: 도시철도법 — Urban Rail and Transportation Law
laws.subtitle: South Korea's world-class public transportation system
laws.fullDescription: South Korea, particularly Seoul, operates one of the world's best metropolitan transit systems. The Seoul Metropolitan Subway has 9 lines, 300+ stations, and carries over 7 million passengers daily. The system is renowned for: near-perfect punctuality, extensive coverage, real-time English/Korean apps, and integrated ticketing (T-money card). South Korea's KTX (Korea Train Express) high-speed rail network connects Seoul to Busan in 2.5 hours at 300 km/h. The Transportation Card Act mandates interoperability between transit systems. South Korea mandates that all transit operators provide barrier-free access for disabled persons, and disability rights activists have staged major subway protest demonstrations demanding better enforcement.
laws.penalty: Transit operators violating safety standards: suspension of service, significant fines. Fraud on transit: fines. ADA equivalent violations: disability rights complaint.
exceptions: Historical lines built before accessibility requirements have modified timelines
Private charter services have different regulations
Freight rail operates under separate rules
laws.sourceLabel: 국토교통부 — Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport

quiz.q: What daily ridership does Seoul's Metropolitan Subway system carry?
quiz.explanation: Seoul's Metropolitan Subway system (operated by Seoul Metro and Korail) carries approximately 7 million passengers daily, making it one of the world's busiest urban transit systems. The system covers Greater Seoul with 9 lines and 300+ stations, offering 24-hour service, real-time apps in multiple languages, and near-perfect punctuality.

laws.title: 가족관계등록법 — Family Registration and Same-Sex Rights
laws.subtitle: South Korea's family law and ongoing LGBTQ+ legal battles
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's family registration system (가족관계등록) records births, marriages, and deaths. Unlike many peer democracies, South Korea does not recognize same-sex marriage or civil unions. However, courts have increasingly recognized rights: the Constitutional Court ruled in 2023 that same-sex couples must be included in national health insurance as dependents — a landmark ruling. Activists have campaigned for decades for marriage equality. South Korea's military criminalizes same-sex acts between soldiers under Article 92-6 of the Military Criminal Act (Constitutional Court found it constitutional in 2023 in a divided vote). Public opinion has shifted significantly — especially among younger Koreans — toward supporting same-sex rights.
laws.penalty: Family registration violations: fines, administrative penalties. Military same-sex acts: up to 2 years imprisonment under Military Criminal Act (Art. 92-6).
exceptions: Court-recognized domestic partnerships receive some benefits (healthcare, housing)
Children born outside marriage have equal inheritance rights since 2013
Foreign same-sex marriages not recognized

quiz.q: What significant 2023 ruling did South Korea's Constitutional Court make regarding same-sex couples?
options: Found same-sex couples must be included in national health insurance as dependents — first major recognition of same-sex rights
Required parliament to vote on marriage equality within 2 years
quiz.explanation: In 2023, South Korea's Constitutional Court ruled that same-sex couples must be included in the National Health Insurance as dependents — a landmark first judicial recognition of same-sex partnership rights in South Korea. While stopping short of marriage equality, the ruling was celebrated by LGBTQ+ advocates as a significant step forward.

laws.title: 출입국관리법 — Immigration Control Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's immigration framework as a major destination for foreign workers
laws.fullDescription: South Korea faces severe demographic challenges — the world's lowest total fertility rate (0.72 in 2023). Immigration is increasingly seen as necessary to address the labor shortage. The Employment Permit System (EPS) manages non-professional foreign workers from 16 partner countries (mostly Southeast Asian). About 2.5 million foreigners live in South Korea (roughly 5% of population). South Korea has been historically monoethnic with limited immigration tradition. Growing multicultural families (결혼이민자 — marriage migrants, mainly women from Vietnam, China, Philippines) have driven some policy evolution. Undocumented foreign workers face crackdowns but also perform essential labor in agriculture and manufacturing.
laws.penalty: Illegal stay over 90 days: deportation, re-entry ban. Employing undocumented workers: criminal fines up to 10 million KRW per worker. Trafficking: up to 10 years imprisonment.
exceptions: F-visa holders (overseas Koreans) have extensive rights approaching citizens
Refugees recognized under the Refugee Act have work authorization
Marriage migrants have special protection pathway to permanent residence

quiz.q: What alarming demographic statistic recorded in South Korea in 2023 is driving increased discussion of immigration policy?
options: South Korea recorded the world's highest elderly population ratio
South Korea recorded a total fertility rate of 0.72 — the world's lowest
South Korea's working-age population overtook retirement-age population for first time
quiz.explanation: South Korea recorded a total fertility rate (TFR) of 0.72 in 2023 — the world's lowest by a significant margin, and far below the replacement rate of 2.1. Seoul's TFR was 0.55. This demographic crisis is projected to halve South Korea's population by 2100 without intervention, driving debate about immigration as a necessary solution.

laws.title: 주택임대차보호법 — Housing Lease Protection Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's unique 'jeonse' rental system and tenant protections
laws.fullDescription: South Korea has a unique rental system called 'jeonse' (전세) — tenants pay a large lump-sum deposit (typically 50-80% of property value) to live rent-free, and landlords use the deposit as investment capital, returning it fully at lease end. This system became problematic when property prices fell — 'jeonse fraud' (전세사기) cases exploded in 2022-2023 as landlords could not return deposits as property values dropped below deposits. Thousands of victims lost billions of KRW. Emergency legislation in 2023 provided victim relief. The Housing Lease Protection Act provides tenant protections: right to two-year lease renewal, rent cap of 5%, and deposit protection priority over mortgages.
laws.penalty: Jeonse fraud: criminal prosecution for fraud. Landlord failing to return deposit: civil enforcement, auction of property. Eviction without cause: damages.
exceptions: New construction has different lease protections
Commercial leases follow separate Commercial Building Lease Protection Act
Luxury apartments above certain price thresholds have modified rules

quiz.q: What is the 'jeonse' system unique to South Korea?
options: A government program providing free housing to newlyweds
A rental system where tenants pay a large lump-sum deposit (50-80% of property value) instead of monthly rent, which the landlord fully returns at lease end
A property tax system paid in lump sums every 5 years
A communal housing arrangement for single young workers
quiz.explanation: Jeonse (전세) is South Korea's unique rental system: tenants provide a large deposit (key money) equivalent to 50-80% of the property's market value and live rent-free. The landlord invests the deposit and returns it in full when the lease ends. The system worked well when property prices rose but collapsed when prices fell in 2022-2023, causing massive jeonse fraud losses.

laws.title: 전자상거래소비자보호법 — E-Commerce Consumer Protection
laws.subtitle: South Korea's strong online consumer rights in a highly digital economy
laws.fullDescription: South Korea is one of the world's most digital economies — with among the highest internet penetration, fastest average internet speeds, and largest e-commerce markets per capita. The E-Commerce Consumer Protection Act provides strong online buyer protections: 7-day no-reason return right (3 months if product is defective), cooling-off period, prohibition of unfair terms in standardized contracts, and strong chargeback rights. Kakao, Naver, Coupang, and international platforms must comply. South Korea has been aggressive in investigating platform monopolies — Kakao faced major antitrust action in 2022-2023. Online fraud and phishing (보이스피싱 voice phishing) is a significant social problem regulated under Financial Crime Prevention Acts.
laws.penalty: False advertising online: fines up to 50 million KRW plus corrective orders. Return right violations: consumer compensation. Platform monopoly abuse: FTC fines up to 10% of revenue.
exceptions: Custom-made products are exempt from the 7-day return right
Digital downloads and services have modified withdrawal rules
B2B platforms have different consumer protection obligations

quiz.q: How long is the general return period for online purchases under South Korea's E-Commerce Consumer Protection Act?
quiz.explanation: South Korea's E-Commerce Consumer Protection Act provides a 7-day 'cooling off' period for online purchases during which consumers can return goods without giving reasons. This extends to 3 months if the seller failed to clearly disclose product defects. South Korea's consumer protection for online commerce is among Asia's strongest.

laws.title: 자원순환기본법 — Resource Circulation Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's advanced waste management and volume-based fee system
laws.fullDescription: South Korea operates one of the world's most sophisticated waste management systems. The Volume-Based Waste Fee System (종량제) requires households to purchase standardized designated bags for waste disposal — making the cost of waste visible. This has reduced landfill waste dramatically since 1995. South Korea has strong food waste recycling — since 2013 food waste must be separated and is composted or converted to animal feed and biogas. Extended Producer Responsibility (생산자책임재활용제도) requires manufacturers to fund recycling of their products. Seoul alone processes over 2 million tons of waste annually. South Korea has among Asia's highest recycling rates (approximately 59%).
laws.penalty: Disposing waste without designated bags: fines. Illegal dumping: criminal fines up to 2 million KRW. Industrial waste violations: business license suspension.
exceptions: Rural agricultural waste has different disposal rules
Construction waste follows separate Waste Disposal Act
Medical waste requires specialized contracted disposal

quiz.q: What innovative waste fee system did South Korea introduce in 1995 that changed household waste behavior?
options: A weekly property tax based on property waste output
Volume-Based Waste Fee — households must buy designated bags for waste, making waste disposal costs proportional to amount generated
quiz.explanation: South Korea's 종량제 (Volume-Based Waste Fee System) requires all households to buy designated official waste bags (available at convenience stores) for their garbage — making waste disposal costs proportional to how much waste one produces. Since its 1995 introduction, South Korea's per-capita waste has significantly decreased and recycling rates have risen dramatically.

laws.title: 성범죄법 / 디지털성범죄 — Digital Sex Crimes Law
laws.subtitle: South Korea's laws against non-consensual photography and deepfake pornography
laws.fullDescription: South Korea passed some of the world's first and strongest laws against 'spycam crimes' (몰래카메라 범죄) and digital sex crimes following massive protests in 2018. The Nth Room case (2019-2020) — where criminal networks extorted sexual content from victims including minors via Telegram — led to the Digital Sex Crime Victims Protection Act. Creating, distributing, or possessing AI-generated deepfake pornography of real people became specifically illegal in 2020. South Korea has a pervasive 'spycam' problem — illegal cameras hidden in restrooms, hotels, and fitting rooms. Dedicated police units were created and convicted perpetrators face sex offender registration.
laws.penalty: Filming in private spaces without consent: up to 7 years. Distributing non-consensual intimate images: up to 7 years. Deepfake sexual content: up to 5 years. All require registration as sex offenders.
exceptions: Consensual adult content with consent verification is legal
Security cameras in designated areas with notices are exempt
Law enforcement surveillance with warrants is authorized

quiz.q: What criminal network case in 2019-2020 triggered major strengthening of South Korea's digital sex crime laws?
options: The Nth Room case — where networks extorted sexual content via Telegram, including from minors
A mass hacking of celebrity accounts
quiz.explanation: The Nth Room (n번방) case involved criminal networks operating on Telegram that extorted and distributed sexual content from victims, including over 70 minors. Operator Cho Ju-bin was sentenced to 42 years. The case shocked South Korea and led to major legislative reforms including specific criminalization of deepfake pornography and stronger investigative powers for digital sex crimes.

laws.title: 언론중재법 / 허위조작정보법 — Press and Disinformation Law
laws.subtitle: South Korea's media regulation and debates over disinformation laws
laws.fullDescription: South Korea has a complex media environment. The Press Arbitration Act (2021 proposed amendment) attempted to impose punitive damages (up to 5x) on media for 'malicious false reporting' — criticized internationally as a threat to press freedom. The law was shelved after widespread media opposition. South Korea's Yonhap News Agency is state-funded. Regulatory bodies KCC (Korea Communications Commission) and KCSC (Communications Standards Commission) regulate broadcasting and online content. Deep political polarization maps onto media — conservative and progressive outlets are sharply divided. Defamation law in South Korea is particularly strict — criminal defamation even for true statements is possible if deemed for improper purposes.
laws.penalty: Criminal defamation (true facts): up to 2 years if for improper purpose. False facts defamation: up to 5 years. Press arbitration awards: significant compensatory damages.
exceptions: Public interest reporting is a defense to defamation
Parliamentary immunity covers statements in National Assembly
Satire clearly labeled as such has some protection

quiz.q: What unusual feature of South Korean defamation law creates concern among press freedom advocates?
options: Criminal defamation can apply even for TRUE statements if the court finds they were made for improper purposes
All defamation claims must be heard by military courts
Foreign journalists are immune from defamation suits
quiz.explanation: South Korea's Criminal Act §307(1) criminalizes defamation by 'making public false facts' but also §307(2) criminalizes 'making public true facts' if done with the purpose of defaming. This means true reporting can constitute criminal defamation if the prosecutor argues improper motive — a provision criticized by press freedom organizations as chilling investigative journalism.

laws.title: 특정 금융거래정보의 보고 및 이용 등에 관한 법률 — Financial Intelligence Act
laws.subtitle: South Korea's AML and cryptocurrency regulation
laws.fullDescription: South Korea is one of the world's largest cryptocurrency markets — South Koreans historically account for 20%+ of global crypto trading volume. The Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information requires crypto exchanges to register with the Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and comply with full AML/KYC requirements. The 'kimchi premium' — the historically higher price of Bitcoin in Korea vs global markets — reflected the closed domestic market. The Terra/Luna collapse (2022) — created by Korean entrepreneur Do Kwon — wiped $40 billion from global crypto markets and triggered criminal charges in South Korea and the US. All crypto-to-fiat conversions require real-name verified bank accounts.
laws.penalty: Unregistered crypto exchanges: criminal prosecution. AML violations: fines up to 300 million KRW. Crypto fraud: prosecution under existing fraud statutes.
exceptions: Institutional crypto trading follows financial product licensing rules
NFTs assessed case-by-case for securities classification
DeFi protocols assessed under new framework being developed

laws.title: 행정심판법 / 행정소송법 — Administrative Appeals and Litigation
laws.subtitle: South Korea's system for challenging government decisions
laws.fullDescription: South Korea's administrative dispute resolution has two tracks: administrative appeal (행정심판) before the Central Administrative Appeals Commission, and administrative litigation (행정소송) before the Administrative Court. Citizens can challenge government permits, sanctions, tax assessments, and immigration decisions. The Administrative Court of Seoul is among Asia's busiest. South Korea's e-government system allows most administrative appeals to be filed online. Landmark administrative cases include challenges to environmental permits for major infrastructure projects, challenges to immigration denials, and disputes over safety regulations. The Administrative Procedure Act requires authorities to give reasons for decisions and notice before adverse decisions.
laws.penalty: Successful appeal: government must comply or pay compensation. Costs typically not awarded against government. Emergency stays available to prevent immediate harm.
exceptions: National security decisions have reduced judicial review
Presidential emergency powers have limited administrative review
Military administrative decisions follow military law

quiz.q: What two methods does South Korea provide for challenging government administrative decisions?
options: Administrative appeal (before administrative commission) and administrative litigation (before Administrative Court)
quiz.explanation: South Korea provides two main pathways for challenging administrative decisions: (1) 행정심판 (administrative appeal) before the Central Administrative Appeals Commission — faster, cheaper, and doesn't require a lawyer; and (2) 행정소송 (administrative litigation) before the administrative courts — more formal with full judicial review. Citizens can typically use either or both in sequence.
